The clue was in the title all along and I just failed to see it.
It's like the studio and creative minds behind this disaster were so stoked with the idea of having Superman and Batman fight each other, they couldn't have a coherent thought after to come up with any form of a story. So they let Zack Snyder make a movie to satisfy the 10 year old in him.
Major spoilers ahead!
I thought there were 3 very strong, compelling ideas from the trailers, but the movie failed to delivery on them
1. Batman's aggression towards Superman. 3/4th of this movie is dedicated to this. In fact Batman wants to KILL Superman. And finally, when the moment arrives, Batman stops because his mother's first name is the same as Superman's mother's. And so they become the best of friends. Just like that.
2. People of earth's distrust of Superman, due to the events from the first movie. This too runs through most of the movie, with Superman trying to earn some brownie points by saving a few people. The fact that there is a public hearing against him, indicates that people are not buying it. But in the end, after his supposed death, why does he a get a military/hero style funeral? Why is the country mourning? Did I miss something? Especially since there is confusion on what happened during the hearing.
3. The public hearing: This should have been a really powerful scene. If Superman were to concede, then he'd be answerable to the people and he would not get to be the hero we know he is. The same, if he did not concede. I was giddy with anticipation when this scene started and was immensely disappointed when the Senator starts mumbling. Zack Snyder took the path of least resistance.
- - - - - -
I guess after the writer's gave up on the main ideas, they didn't care about smaller plot points
- Superman has no remorse for the destruction he caused in the first movie. In the big fight he smashes Batman through a building causing the building to collapse. Ditto for Doomsday, smashes him in to a power plant of some sort. He is not even thinking about anyone's safety.
- Just like in the first movie, there is an apocalypse level destruction. Superman himself contributes to some of it. Thousands are probably killed, but superman only saves Lois Lane
- Superman threatens Batman that he can easily kill Batman, twice. Sounds like a bully to me
- Batman STEALING from Lex Luthor so HE gets to exact revenge on Superman
- Batman uses guns, not to intimidate, but actually kill. He even dreams of gun battles.
- The govt. has Zod's body and the ship for 2 years. Luthor comes up with the idea that since the ship has a bio-metric security, he can use Zod's body to gain access. It did not cross anyone else's mind
- One alien craft/tech is lying in the Indian Ocean for 2 years. No nation/military has claimed it. Local fishermen are freely swimming to it and breaking away pieces
- The all powerful Kryptonian key has no security what so ever. Anyone can use it. Even Lex Luthor. It only unlocks EVERYTHING, why should it be secure?
- Kryptonians have banned the technology to create Doomsday. It's so dangerous, they decide not to remove it from the system but keep it, with so minimum security that it can be enabled with a simple voice command by a non-Kryptonian.
- There is no compelling reason behind Lex Luthor's hatred towards Superman. How does he stand to gain or lose?
- There is no villain, purpose, motive or problem to solve in the story. Doomsday appears so that Zack Snyder can once again have a city-leveling battle.
- Why is Doomsday angry with Superman? Since he is made from Zod & Luthor's genes, does anger/hatred towards someone pass through genes?
- When Batman steals the Kryptonite, it would have spoiled whatever Luthor had planned, but Luthor just eggs Superman to fight Batman like they were in cahoots. How does Luthor know what Batman has planned? How does he know about the battle royale. Has he read the comic?
- Why is Batman not suspicious of the other meta beings? Why does he think they are friendly and will help? And against what? Why does he think he will need their help? How come Luthor is in on this?
- Why does Luthor have well designed logos for each meta human?
- Why was wonder woman so concerned with being exposed? According to the photo, she had already revealed herself, in FULL COSTUME. So why the secrecy? And why come out of hiding when she sees lightening coming from the dome? She did not feel the need when world was practically getting destroyed in the first movie.
- Why does Luthor introduce Bruce Wayne and Clark Kent to each other? BW is a billionaire, but CK? Why would anyone care about him?
- Superman stops the car chase. Literally allowing the bad guys to escape. He may not like Batman's methods, but he couldn't figure out if Batman's giving a chase, he's after bad guys?!
- In the midst of deafening destruction Superman can hear Lois Lane. But his mother...his hearing, speed, x-ray vision...he doesn't even give it a shot. And of course Batman finds her in a jiffy because he is...
... the list goes on...but IMDb has a word limit...
I can't believe such a high profile movie had no thought put behind it. Amateur hour. A total disservice to a 75 year legacy and to the fans. I hope the remaining DC movies are scrapped or they finally pulls their socks up.

The important thing to remember about Telltale games is that they aren't about creating a branching and hugely divergent narrative tree. Most of their games usually have a story that they want to tell and you immerse yourself in that story by shaping relationships with characters through dialogue in action.
Many reviewers have said that choices don't matter and that the ending is rushed and unfulfilling. On both counts I would have to respectfully disagree. The choices really do matter, in the last couple of episodes especially. A lot of times the payoff isn't immediate, but how you act shapes the dialogue and how other characters react to you throughout the game. The ending is in fact leading to a sequel but it in no way feels rushed or tacked on. It actually seems like Telltale didn't have enough time to tell the expansive narrative they want to tell and need a second season to do so. That's fine because this first season had legitimately good storytelling and they do a good job setting up for the sequel.
The storytelling is the crucial part of a Telltale game, and let me tell you, this one does not disappoint. It's just as bleak, tense, and gut wrenching as the TV show and books and the moments where you had to navigate the minefield of diplomacy without making a misstep were genuinely well done.
I have to point out that there are some weird graphical and texture glitches that pop up from time to time, but generally don't kill the mood sense they go by so quickly. Also on the topic of graphics, I think the aesthetic of this game will be really hit or miss. I, personally, liked the watercolor style but I could see where someone else might think it just looks bad.
The game is great if you want a really well written, tense, and gut wrenching narrative that really captures the feeling of Game of Thrones. As long as you know that Telltale has an overarching narrative in place and your choices serve more to further character development and deepen the sense of immersion, you won't be disappointed.

Game of Thrones is an episodic point and click adventure game developed and published both by Telltale Games in 2014. Game of thrones follows the Show's story from Season 3 onward so if you havent watched it up to that point then dont play this. Game of Thrones uses a pastel art style and makes every background and setting a work of art. This can make the characters feel kinda blurry at times but overall it works incredibly well and fits with the theme. You play from the point of multiple different characters but all from House Forrester. House Forrester is a house who was loyal to Robb Stark and is now in the spotlight after his fall at the Red Wedding. Forresters are known for their ability to harvest a special kind of wood called Ironwood that's exclusive to the forresters lands. Your goal is to keep your house alive, mainly through using Ironwood as leverage. The developers really made this feel like an actual game of thrones world and that can mean only one thing: No happy endings.
The story in game of thrones is made to the utmost perfection with a plot that has some of the best moments I've ever experienced in a game. There are some battles where you'll be cheering along with the soldiers and the game does an excellent job of inspiring you in ways I never thought possible. The characters that Telltale has made here are incredibly in-depth and this enhances the game in many ways. The environments each have their own extensive story: The Ironwood halls of Ironwrath, the vipers pit of King's Landing, and even the frosty tundra of Castle Black each is brimming with lore and backstory.The story itself is made in true GoT style with loads of death and brimming with plot twists and suprises. The story definitely had me with some unexpected turns and really immersed me in the world so that I began to seriously care about what's happening. The art style blends well enough into the game to where it feels like you're playing a painting come to life. Now I need to adress the main flaw with this game and really for all other Telltale games for that matter: The illusion of choice. In GoT you are presented throughout the game with lots of different decisions that seem to have different outcomes. In reality, the choices you make will still follow main plot points no matter what so really most of your choices mean absolutely nothing and are just there to make you seem in control. This is apparent very early in the game when a main character is killed no matter what you do and in the end this just makes you feel powerless and ultimately like your choices mean nothing. The main thing your choices give you is a different bit of dialogue at the end when your choices are being discussed. Overall the only reason I can overlook this even just a little bit is that the story here is so phenomenal that it's still good even with this issue shadowing it. Even with this as a glaring issue this is still one of the best stories I've ever had the pleasure of experiencing and, without spoiling much, I can say that if you're expecting a happily-ever-after type ending then you'll be very disappointed.
Telltale's Game of Thrones is an inspiring story of heroism and betrayal that stays true to it's roots and makes sure that you wont leave with your feelings intact.

This Review is of Single Player only, when I try multiplayer I will update the review
I've played Story mode and Arcade mode and will be basing my review on those.
First of all this game looks great, sure there's a lot of pixel games out there, but this one manages to stand out by having some distinguishing marks like the cut scenes and original art. So when you play the game you don't feel like you're "just playing yet another so and so", it's draws you in.
The game play is very fast paced, and similar to games like Nuclear Throne, Relic Hunter Zero and many other such games that have recently showed up on steam (I feel like Nuclear Throne marked the trend, but maybe it's because it was the first such game that interested me, so I didn't notice any before it). What makes the game play in in Fistful of Gun hence force FoG very interesting is the level of variance in each protagonist you play. Many games try to make their characters unique but fail to, this game like Risk of Rain before it has achieved it effortlessly. When you play Arcade mode you can see just how different each one of the heroes is from the others. You have snipers, with strong but slow single shots, you got some aoe champs, you have control champs, you have your gatling monsters, and they all have strengths and weaknesses making them all viable, interesting, and challenging.
There was one little problem for me, I played the game with a keyboard and mouse, and that made 3 of the characters very impractical, that is the first one, billy and one more, where I have just way too many things to handle in quick succession, and need to move my hand on the keyboard, I'd say a controler is definitely helpful for this game.
I liked the level of customization available for the key bindings, the graphics, and other options.
There is one little thing that some people might hate, and others might love, I personally found it handy. You can get out of an area by just getting to the exit, I found that out by accident, just by walking too close to the edge and accidentally getting out. Some people will hate leaving a place they didn't want to leave in the heat of battle. But on the other hand it means you can bail out on impossible situations, and also speed run the game (provided you're nimble enough).

The most stupid tactical game I have played in my life. I've seen stupid but not this bad.
-Raising difficulty level only means your soldiers miss more, and that a 75% hit chance will hit one out of 4-5 times at max.
-Psychology is the most random and unthoughtful addition to the game one could imagine: soldiers at random will shoot the enemy that is PTSDing them and crit OR shoot one of your own OR hunker down, all of which are actions added to their own in a game which logic revolves entirely around actions/round.
-You can run and shoot, but not shoot and run - no sense at all. And this is actually a huge thing in this game. So a mechanic that has no sense is constantly affecting the game - not cool
-The tech tree could very well be a linear progress with no choices, as you find out that the ressources required for upgrades come in an ordre and amount that forces you into a specific order
-Snipers miss ALL THE TIME before they reach a threshold of exp at which point they never miss, No progression. Plus why is the sniper guy (who is heavily penalised for his accuracy by his limited movement) the one with the worst aim?
-The construction of facilities, just like the tech tree, gives an illusion of choice since the rest of the game pushes you in one direction, not penalizing other directions but prohibiting them altogether (you don't have enough this or that, hey why not build THIS thingy!). This makes games all the same (except if you play easy levels - but even there you are still limited), except for matters of no importance.
-Many glitches
-Graphism is shameful for a game of this age, animations are very often ridiculous. With the skill level of this company, an isometric game should have been the plan.
-The move+actions/round is ridiculous and tactically inferior to, say, an action point system: if a guys sprints in a round, he should not shoot in the same way (number of shots or bullets, accuracy, etc.) as the guy that stood where he was and shot the whole round.
-Overwatch is ridiculous because enemies need to be moving in your line of sight for you to shoot at them. So, for instance if a enemy rushes to a corner from which he can see you, he will then proceed to move away from his cover to take aim and shoot at your face while your guy on overwatch is like "well, he's not moving (from tile to tile) in my line of sight, so I won't shoot", even though the enemy is in clear sight. This is a big factor because enemis won't run in front of you, they will run to another cover and shoot at you making overwatch essentially useless.
-Your soldiers will not always use the cover next to them, and will sometimes stay up like tourists at the end of their turn without you having any option to change that
-Your guys cannot kneel or lay down on command for more cover
-you cannot shoot at objects/walls to blow thing up. So if an enemy hides behing a giant bomb, your solider will refuse to shoot at anything because he "has no target". He will have a take 10 turns to surround the bomb or close in on the bomb to see the guy.
-Close range (I mean pointing the gun to the face of the enemy) will miss at a ridiculous rate, once again except for higher level soldiers.
-Your squad is absurdly small (4, then 5 and then 6 soliders), which is absolutely not compensated by customization of loadouts (caracter classes - which you do not choose, FYI - totally lock your soldiers in one type of weapon), or of appearance (OMG the graphics are so awful!). Your soliders can carry ONE grenade, or ONE medikit, or ONE vest - like they have ONE pocket OR room enough to wear a vest - what?
All of this -and more- makes for a very frustrating gaming experience. I still played it because I wanted it so bad to be a noble heir of the XCom family, but it's really, really not. Just a sad, sad game in the end. Never been as underwhelmed for a new game as XCom 2 - which looks just as awful (it's 2016 guys, really?) and seems to have the same stupid mechanics.

If you like twin stick shooters, this game is alright. I'd say it it's nothing to write home about but it's at least decent. I'd recommend it on sale for sure and if you have a thing for solo (can't speak for splitscreen) twinstick shooters you'd probably like this.
Pros:
I'm not going to write a list, so if you're lazy go ahead and scroll down to another review. Visually, the game is about what you'd expect from a $20 twinstick shooter, it's a "pro" because it doesn't fail to deliver. The game hits the same bar on sound, enemy design and gameplay mechanics in my opinion as well. I only played the survival mode (more my thing) and I enjoyed my time once I got beyond the first few games where I was underleveled, underskilled, unaware and just bad. Learning when to call in what support is important and I think is a nice element of the survival gamemode. Avoiding bringing big enemies in to the best of your ability while also still trying to get things you need/want can make for some intense situations. Overall I can't say enough about the gameplay, it's a solid twinstick with very minor RPG elements.
Cons:
The problems I have with this game are pretty simple. The game has like 4 survival maps and I've only been able to find weapon spawns on one single map. I also found that it's easiest to do one or two of the maps over the others just due to difficulty and the ability to set up easier. Hanger would break more often than not for me and wouldn't let me finish (though I reported it and a dev said they're fixing it.. might've been fixed already). Aside from having a pathetic amount of maps to pick from the classes also feel incredibly limited. You get 3 slots and for the majority of the classes you only get 1 class skill. What this means is all 4 classes share 2 trees, one passives and one abilities, and everybody is going to end up with 2/3 abilities coming from the one tree. For me it boiled things down to "do I want a limited fire turret, a forced flamethrower or two weapons and a regular turret with an ammo cap that's super low?
The other massive problem I have with the game that's entirely subjective is: I don't understand why multiplayer isn't a thing. I'd easily double or triple my time and at least 2 of my friends would've bought the game if there was multiplayer. The game is PERFECT for multiplayer even with the handful of maps but it's just flat not there. From what I understand it's not entirely off the table but there are other priorities and I'm just assuming multiplayer won't ever happen. I know there are a lot of "gaem needs mp" gripes but it's for a reason. Add a DLC that adds 2 maps, a class and MP and I'm sure you'd get a $5-10 price range. It's just sad because the game is great but I can't experience it with friends.
I'd say the game is a solid 7/10 at least.

I can't explain how this game makes me feel. But if I could sum it up in one sentence it is: Don't judge someone until you've walked a mile in their shoes.
The main character, tired of their current way of life, moves to a new town, and, due to the meeting of a mysterious stranger, she experiences the lives of four citizens, all in different stages of their lives:
Katherin - A crazy cat lady who sees Santa Claus hallucinations.
The Nurse - A dementia-stricken nurse.
Mabel - A serial killer who tries to mask the poisoning of her husband.
Mr. Green - A grumpy old man who is mean-spirited, and refuses to support his family.
In the end, the player ultimately decides the fate of the lives of all four characters. The choices the players make ultimately decides how the game ends.
The graphics and sound effects are reminiscent of classic RPGs such as Earthbound and Shining Force. The game is relatively short, but requires multiple playthroughs to achieve all three endings.

With a great scenery and beautiful graphics, Dying Light is easily the best looking zombie game out there. The story of Dying Light is really generic, but the characters and the protagonist make up for that. Dying Light has a decent sized city to play in and gives you a new city to play in further into the game. Free running over the roofs and many obstacles in the city of Harran feels awesome and really smooth. Combat could use a bit more depth but has some really smooth dodging mechanics to keep it fun, and make it challenging at times. There's also a nice upgrading/crafting system for your weapons and creating fun gadgets like Throwing stars and Fireworks. Leveling is really fun aswell, you have 3 different skill tree's which you level up at the same time and some really nice skills to unlock. Looting and lockpicking is fun but in the end not really worth it most of the time.
The A.I. of the zombies is decent and the game has good cinematics and voice acting. However the mainstory is a bit short and the ending is kinda dissapointing, i'm not going to spoil anything but first of all the last mision can't be played co-op. This is big let down for someone who played through the whole game with a friend. Also the final boss is a quick time event, which makes it even more dissapointing.
Even though the game has some downsides, overall this game is alot of fun. And it succeeds at what it tries to do,  Being one of the best zombie games out there. I would definitely recommend Dying Light to anyone that loves free roaming zombie games.

great game 10/9. but didn't know what to review so instead i made this peanut butter-chocolate cookie recipe.
INGREDIENTS
1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, (spooned and leveled)
1 teaspoon baking soda
1 cup peanut butter (smooth or chunky)
4 tablespoons ( 1/2 stick) unsalted butter, room temperature
1/2 cup packed dark-brown sugar
1/2 cup granulated sugar
2 large eggs
1 teaspoon pure vanilla extract
8 ounces semisweet chocolate, cut into chunks
DIRECTIONS
Preheat oven to 350 degrees. In a bowl, whisk together flour and baking soda; set aside. In a large bowl, using an electric mixer, beat peanut butter, butter, and sugars until light and fluffy. Add eggs and vanilla, and beat until smooth. With mixer on low, gradually add flour mixture, beating just until combined. Stir in chocolate chunks.
Drop dough by heaping tablespoons, 1 inch apart, onto two large baking sheets. Bake until golden, 13 to 15 minutes, rotating sheets halfway through. Transfer cookies to wire racks to cool.

Bohemia Interactive have opted for a simulator-style flight model that has more emphasis on enjoyment with a 'feeling' of realism, rather than a full-on realistic helicopter simulation. This was a good decision, as helicopters are inherently difficult to fly. For the average gameplayer, this would almost certainly lead to frustration... Not a good recipe for entertainment.
The flight model they have opted for takes many of the helicopter's tricker flight dynamics and tones it down to a more manageable set of rules. There are three different difficulty modes, each offering more than enough of a challenge. The easiest mode adds a generous level of automatic corrections to flight, as well as a few extra navigational aids etc. while still maintaining a challenge.
With an added storyline to follow to spice things up, Take On Helicopters is a refreshing addition to a stagnant flight sim market and one that I highly recommend!

Definitely one of Telltale Games must haves. The game itself runs well and the mechanics are the same as with any other Texas Hold 'Em Poker game you would run in to, but what makes this game worthwhile is the characters you play against. Max, The Heavy, Strong Bad & Tycho share hilarious, well-written banter between each other and the player, making it fun to stick around and play just to see what they will start babbling about next. Obviously a fair amount of banter is humour and in-jokes from their respective games/web-series, but is done in a way so it is still amusing to those who are not familiar with their respective Franchises. Another nice touch is the range of reactions the characters have to actions the player has. For example going All-In, depending on the situation, can cause the whole table to turn and look at you with suprise and shout. Alternitively the characters will also act smug if they have the upper hand, or get angry or frustrated if you are winning that hand. All in all, this is one of the most funny and interesting Poker Sims to play, and worth having for the occasional hand of Poker, with a table of characters who are very much, insane.

Welcome to the wild wild west, a place of outlaws and gunslingers. Clayton Boon made a deal with the devil to crush anyone who opposed his railroad company, however, "he didn't count on The Righteous Psychosis of those he had wronged" A Fistful of Gun is a fast pace, arcade-style, top-down shooter with a wild west theme. Choose a character, go on a killing spree and ultimately get to Boon. Watch out not to shoot any of the people in the neutral area's (unless you want to earn some extra money or lives), because you will have an unstoppable sheriff after you, or getting thru the next level with a humiliating handicap, like an explosive piñata strapped on your back. It is a difficult game to master, keep your eyes open for scattered power-ups and you might just make it out alive.
At the beginning of the game you can pick from 3 different characters out of a total of 11 which you need to unlock in story mode, each with their own control set, for example: Noah uses the keyboard, while playing Abel you need an XBOX 360 controller, making it all that easier to play local co-op. Not only are the controls different per character, but reloading is done differently per character as well, making it interesting to try out other characters. A Fistful of Gun allows online or local co-op multiplay with up to eight players.
What is most enjoyable, is the game music, it has a certain western/arcade flair.
PROS
+ Awesome game music,
+ Fun arcade-style top-down shooter,
+ Challenging,
+ Easy controls for local co-op.
CONS
- Becomes repetitive.

I'm having a lot of fun with A Fistful of Gun. You play as one of eleven characters, each with their own unique weaponry. From shotguns, to pistols, to miniguns, to explosives, you have a variety of different ways to play. You need to adjust your playthrough depending on which character you choose.
The combat and shooting is very nice. This is a bullet-hell esque game where you have to avoid the enemy bullets while killing the enemy. There are different kinds of enemies that require different approaches; Some enemies are killed with one shot, while others are more tanky and take more than one hit.
One thing this game could improve on is creating a tutorial, because it throws you into the combat so suddenly. There are no explanations on what you are supposed to do, or where you're supposed to go. The controls could be made a lot clearer. The first few times I died, it wasn't just because I sucked at the game but because I literally had no idea what I was supposed to do. It would be nice to practice my character a bit before being thrown in-game. However the controls are fairly easy to grasp after a few deaths or so since this game is fast-paced, so you get used to what you have to do fairly quickly.
In the story mode, you start out in a neutral area where you progress by choosing a direction of the screen to go to. You have a general idea of what you're going to do next by the small picture describing what's there. You start with seven lives, and you can gain more by collecting playing cards that you occasionally come upon. You could go to a railroad area, a river, play a card game, meet a merchant, push a cart, save some hostages, unlock a new player, get ambushed, and more.
I know a lot of reviewers aren't recommending this game based off the story mode, but I had fun playing alone. That being said, this game is more fun with friends, so I recommend finding friends to play with. There are not a lot of people playing online, so it's difficult playing an online match.
This game is polished, well made, and a lot of fun to play. I definitely recommend picking this up if you're looking for a fun co-op game to play with friends.

It is with a very heavy heart I write this review. First and foremost I am a huge fan of TellTale and their work but I cannot in good conscience recommend this game. I'll  touch first on what this game does right, In my opinion it nails the atmosphere of Game of Thrones. The plotting, the schemeing the backbiting, you see it all firsthand. I'm also a fan of the art style, I like the hand drawn cel-shaded effect. Now, let me elabrate on what I didn't like. First like any other TellTale game your choices do not change the out come of the story, only the means you get to the end. Think of it as several paths to the same end, more or less, there can be some minor differences but on the whole the story goes the same. *Walking Dead spoiler* (Like the end of The Walking Dead Season 1, Lee dies no matter your desicions.) Second thing I didn't like, and probably most infuriating to me,giving characters from the novel/TV show major roles in this game. I do not like it because those characters cannot be changed, because they are written into the stone of the canon, therefore you cannot kill them or change their motives. If they had played merely cameo roles then I would have understood, but putting these characters into major roles pretty much defeats the "your choices matter" line. Alan Wake's American Nightmare was a great game to play.
In comparison to the first- not everything is clouded in darkness, there are way more guns, the engine as a whole feels much, MUCH, more polished and fluid. There are also live action cut scenes which I thought were awesome!! I felt it brought the characters to life in a fun and authentic feeling way. The characters for Mr. Scratch, Alan, and Alice all looked very, very similar to their in-game rendered model.
Starting with the guns & fighting: You now have multiple small arms and multiple long arms, similar to the 2 weapon slots in the first game. For small arms you have a nail gun, either an uzi or mac10, revolver, and 9mm semiauto. Long guns had the double barrel & pump shotguns, an M16, M4A1, crossbow, and hunting rifle. These are the ones I can remember off the top of my head, there may have been a few more, and a few I didn't unlock. The guns feel fairly good shooting, ammo was much too plentiful in the game as there are caches of ammo & batteries for the flashlight all over the place as you play. The flashlight was also changed in American Nightmare to no longer give the constant damage to the enemies's shield, handy when you're low or facing a single enemy, now you have to boost the flashlight to do any shield damage. The flashlight recharges super fast, however, and I rarely, rarely used batteries compared to the first game (also no flashlight upgrades).
The enemies in this game were not too difficult, most still had shields and they actually made a few enemies have different mechanics than the first game which was greatly appreciated. The process of burning down the shield and plinking at the same human silhouettes got old quickly in the first. This introduces enemies who fly around as crows and turn into humans, attempting to ambush and avoid your gun fire, enemies who split if you focus your flashlight on them, and even spiders who die by gun fire or light, no shield made of darkness.
Where the first game had great settings and characters, the 2nd falls flat. There are 3 locations for the whole game which was intended for the story, but man was it boring. Luckily each time you revisit a location the tasks at hand are fast forwarded a bit so you spend a lot less time in each area upon returning. There were 3 intractable characters you worked with during the game: a mechanic Emma (boring and over sexualized in appearance), an astrologer/scientist Dr. Rachel Meadows (also over sexualized in appearance), and a theater attendant/film maker named Serena (this time over sexualized via EXTREMELY sIutty dialogue). Mr. Scratch, your bestie, is the 4th character you really do anything with and he's pretty freakin funny in this game, I got a kick out of his♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥bagginess and his bad guy antics.
I did not play nor had any interest in the survival/arena mode which seems to be a highlight in this game.
To sum up AW vs AL:AN- Alan Wake has a better setting, story, and characters. Alan Wake: American Nightmares has a better game engine, graphics, guns, and enemies.
I recommend both, it's just too bad they couldn't get the best of both games together.

I was really hyped to get this game back a few months when I saw some banner promotions around the internet (I was a fan of the previous game) Sadly I lost track of time and lost the title in the mix of all the other games that came out around the same time this one did. Luckily I was reminded of the game by a friend who gave me a key to try the game out. The way steam has their review system made it really hard for me to figure out which category (yes or no) I should put this game under for recommendation. The review system needs a neutral option. Anyway I shall get to the point and not bore you guys with me rambling on.
Positives:
- An interesting learning curve since the diffculty even on normal is challenging. A player can't just blast through all their ammo with no regrets like you think youd be able to especially on the first level of the game. Instead you have to watch your ammo count (since all your guns are on shared ammo) and notice your surroundings since you can easily corner yourself.
- The skill system is actually a plus since theres quite a few different combinations one can do which effects the gameplay quite decently.
- A diffculty scale on top of the screen which gives you a general indication on what to expect.
- Each class feels different (not at first but about mid way of the game).
- The survival mode is a fun addition to the game. It offers a bit more then the campaign in the sense of fun and intense combat.
- The bullet registry is pretty good to where I haven't run into an issue of shooting something and it just not hitting.
- The different combinations of skills with weapons makes the gameplay quite fresh for a twin stick shooter.
- Boss kills feel extremely satisfying since the battles require you to think quickly and approach it in a different way then the previous boss you fought.
Negative Points
-  The game is short and feels like a dlc. (One i'd pay $10-15 for)
- No online coop (that's what pushed this game out of my mind since I love to play games like this with friends)
- Voice acting is cheezy and cringy from time to time (more times then I would want it to be)
- The ammo system i'm mixed about I like it but hate it since all weapon's ammo is tied together meaning you really have to watch how much you shoot and make sure to pick up that ammo whenever you can
- The responsiveness when interacting with ammo crates/hp crates feels a little slow to where sometimes it takes about 2-3 seconds more then it should to interact with them (That doesnt sound terribly bad but it when getting swarmed and your low on ammo or health it turns into a really bad situation).
- Can't change the mouse sensitivity (This one is more of a personal negative point, since I play on a high sensitivity not being able to change it ended up frustrating the hell out of me at first but I eventually adjusted).
- Sometimes the diffculty feels much harder then it should be in some parts then becomes insanely easy in other parts.
With all of that being said the game is something I plan on playing here and there. The game has some good points and some faults but not enough faults to make me regret spending time on the game. The game itself is priced a little high I personally believe it should be $10-15, which means if you are thinking of getting it wait until theres a sale. In the end it just feels like a weaker helldivers but still a game worth trying.

Even if it is only remotely considered a sequel to The Red Solstice, today I’m reviewing Solstice Chronicles: MIA, a game that can stand on its own and can be enjoyed by veterans and new players of the series alike. It’s the second Steam project for developer Ironward, but they decided to drop the squad-based shooting (Co-Op or AI assisted) in favor of either a two-player formula or lone wolf and drone assistance. Along with new maps and foes, Solstice Chronicles: MIA also expands the leveling system from its predecessor.
The game defines irony quite well. Humanity fled Earth after it was compromised by the STROL virus and the mutants it created. Mars, the eternal Red Planet and eventually a colony in real life (not that we’ll live long enough to see it) seems like the logical choice for a Sci-Fi setting that is as close to a hellscape as it can ever get. The fourth planet from the Sun was also overrun by STROL-infused monsters which made short work of both the colonists and the security detail. Players assume the role of a lone survivor, a grunt whose name is never revealed and he’s being refered to as “Marine”. Not even a Joe or Bob, Ironward? I’ll call him Billy, then. MIA is the acronym for "missing in action". A step above KIA, but only because of uncertainty.
At least we’re told of our Marine’s employer. The Elysium Mining Corporation may not be the unseen evil in this title, so they’re not comparable to Umbrella, Tyrell or Weyland-Yutani. They certainly don’t try to “harness” or better said, weaponize the monsters for some devious purpose, but can still be accused of minimizing the threat or not providing the marines with enough firepower to have a fighting chance. It was a turkey shoot and once the chocolate cake has hit the fan, you can expect no reinforcements either. Marine Dude has to evacuate his hind from the accursed planet and he’ll have to do it on his own. Or almost, since he quickly finds himself in the company of a mysteriously chatty drone that calls herself “Saffron” (yes, she has a female voice).
So at least Solstice Chronicles: MIA knows how to sprinkle some comic relief over the otherwise prevalent survival horror subplots and themes. It isn’t even an escort mission since Saffron can assist the Marine in more ways than one. I shall focus on her skills in the gameplay section and for now I will summarize the 22 levels within the game, while avoiding spoilers. Marine flees for his life but the plot obviously thickens as he discovers that the colony's demise has been deliberate. An inside job, a resistance movement which reminded me of the Red Faction series (it’s on Mars, right?) and the increasingly numerous swarms of mutants, are just some of the obstacles between one hapless but glorified bodyguard and his shuttle towards home. Wherever that might be, since Earth is no longer a valid destination.
I know the drill. Unreal Engine 4 and 4K resolution@60fps aren’t getting along very well. I went for 2K but even then I had several instances in which the frame rate would drop close to 30fps. Fortunately, it didn’t happen during the majority of the gameplay. By the time you get zerg rushed by dozens of foes at the same time, you’re chances of survival are slim already. On the upside, UE4 does provide adequate eye candy if the dev team was skilled enough. Ironward confirmed this unwritten rule. The levels may seem like few but they are filled to the brim with details and asset reuse or not, they are never positioned in a similar manner as to provoke a déjà vu. Particle and lighting effects, excellent shooting animations and a convincing (albeit fictional) flamethrower trajectory, it all feels and looks like a quality game. I played my fair share of twin stick shooters over the years but Solstice Chronicles: MIA is definitely one of the prettier titles within the genre. It even features cinematics rendered with the in-game engine, instead of FMVs (pre-recorded animations).
Surprisingly, there’s little to complain about the sounds as well. Voice acting was fine, if nothing special. But at least  they didn’t hire actors who phoned in their dialogue. Yeah, I know that drone looks like the infamous “Dinklebot” from Destiny, but I assure you that Saffron is far more enthusiastic in her line delivery. Soundtrack never bothered me and the sound effects were on par with the rest of the audio assets.
Several key elements separate Solstice Chronicles: MIA from its competitors on Steam. Apart from the good looks, the gameplay really shines through the use of that drone in conjunction with a single marine controlled by the player or a two-man team in Co-Op. A Threat Level gauge indicates at all times, an accurate estimation of both the scale and sheer power of the mutant swarm trying to chew your face off at that specific moment and location. Threat Level elevates itself as you slay more and more approaching foes but it can also be lowered by scripted events or Saffron’s direct intervention since her Taunt skill is used precisely for this reason. Her other abilities (Scout, Block, Bomb) are just as useful in the long run. Just don’t forget that you aren't fighting this “uphill battle” alone and that the AI doesn’t get between you and your marks nor does it require babysitting, since the mutants prefer Marine flesh over a chunk of metal and circuit boards.
Our not-so-silent protagonist has a deadly skillset of his own, but it is more dependent on player choice. Character classes are represented by Assault, Demolition, Hellfire and Terminator. The first two are rather self-explanatory and too “vanilla” for my tastes so I went with Hellfire since Terminator is a bonus class unlocked after you’ve completed the 22nd level on the Normal (“Soldier")  difficulty. If it isn’t obvious already, Hellfire is the “Flamethrower Guy”. The weapons are well diversified in comparison to enemy variety or methods of dispatching them. The class I chose had the second weapon slot locked to the Salamander P20 Flamer and that also happens to be my favorite weapon in the game. Mutant BBQ from a seemingly endless ammo supply, as the flamethrower is reliant on the Marine’s stamina. Weird choice but fortunately most stats can be upgraded in the game’s RPG-like leveling system. Skill points get distributed between missions.
I mentioned that the tactics seem rather limited and the shooting mechanics within Solstice Chronicles: MIA gets repetitive when you know that the foes follow a liniar pattern. A beeline towards the protagonist. No ambushing, flanking and the vast majority of mutants don’t have a ranged attack option of their own. So they just try to close in on our armed-to-the-teeth Marine by mindlessly charging in hope that numbers alone will suffice. It gets old eventually and the boss fights are few and far in-between. You’ll be tossing flares almost as frequently as grenades, since most levels are too dark and you’ll be hearing the swarms sooner than spotting them. It adds to the horror element so I can’t complain. A desolated colony shouldn’t light up like a Christmas tree after all. The environments vary from collapsed highways to sewers and laboratories. They all have in common the green STROL infested areas that also double as mutant spawning locations.
As with other titles from the genre, the more you use a specific weapon, the bigger bonuses you get in regards to damage or reload speed. And you’ll have quite an arsenal to choose from, so at least the firearms don’t disappoint as much as the mutants themselves. Overall, Solstice Chronicles: MIA is a worthy sequel and a step in the right direction for the developer. Perhaps Solstice will become a trilogy since it’s already a series  which proves that even twin stick shooters can move with the times.

Great Twin-Stick Shooter with several different game modes.  It looks nice and gets the basic gameplay down while adding an almost horror-ish element with many dark areas only visable through your flashlight.... which can only shine one direction at once.  Think "Dead Nation" if anyone has played that but replace zombies with..... alienish space monsters and some... space zombies?  Good enemy variety and 4 different classes- each with varying skill trees.  Nice variety of main weapons, usable items, class-based special abilities/items, and "heavy" items including the lovable Flamethrower, Charged-Beam-Type-Uber-Cannon, Explosive-Heavy-Launcher-Type-Deal.... you get the deal.  I've mostly messed around with the campaign (which would play a bit differently with other classes- so I'm looking forward to subsequent playthroughs) but there is a Survival Mode.... I've only messed with it a little bit but you are on a large map and are to do certain objectives in order to get an evac-ship.  There are defensive structures to build and all the campaign's weapons and goodies are present..... I believe you must have a seperate character in Survival Mode so your weapon progress and leveling up/skill trees would start from scratch.
There is some RPGish-ness here, too, which I LOVE.... you level up your ability with weapons.... so while the regular Assault Rifle might not have as much punch as the LMG, you might have enough levels into the AR to make it worthwhile over the agruably better LMG.  The skill tree has the basics such as more speed, health, faster reloading and whatnot- but there are some cool gamechangers... I can't speak for all the skill-trees, but the Assault Tree has a Cluster Bomb ability that would replace your "Main" class ability, beit the Enhanced Ammo or Crazy-Fire-Explosive-Mine.... you can upgrade the Cluster Bomb to explode over a larger area, do more damage, and cooldown quicker to allow for more usage.  You have a drone companion that houses some of the more unique features of this game.  You have a "threat" meter.... which is pretty self-explanatory.  Different actions can increase or decrease the meter.  I believe it slowly goes up over time but you can have your drone go collect supplies for you in exchange for an increased threat meter.... the drone can also put down an energy shield to stop/slow enemies and place a SUPERHUGE bomb that can wipe out huge areas.  Your last ability, Taunt, decreases the Threat meter BUT will immediately spawn enemies based on how high your Threat meter is..... so it becomes a balancing act of how far you can push or what locations you think you can hold off a hoarde and thus use Taunt.  It's a neat system that, once you understand it, can greatly help with both enjoyment and survival.
When done correctly I tend to enjoy Twin-Stick-Shooters..... especially when they have some RPG-elements.  Solstice Chronicles: MIA gets the gameplay down and adds enough little twists to make this quite a fun and potentially high-hour game.  I'm looking forward to finishing my initial campaign as the Assault Dude and then playing through as a Demolitions Guy and the third class..... which I believe is a "Slow but Heavily Armored" type.  The 4th class is unlocked after you beat the campaign on a certain difficulty and I don't know much about it.  Highly recommended if you like Twin-Stick Shooters.... I really LOVE Dead Nation and this is a game I'd put up there with DN.

the physics in this game are also pretty amazing (yes they bounce! ok now that ive gushed so much about the graphics its time for the gameplay.  simply put the gameplay is meh.  for those of you that are thinking its going to be a zelda ish combat of dodging bosses and cutting grass you would be dissapointed.  only certain monsters will actualy need to bother with dodging and thats only if you havent been leveling your gear.  though the dodge system is there and is useful you only truly get to use it end game (which is annoying for training noobs on it because dodging should be numero uno)  most enemies can be dealt with by simply spaming attacks and mild amounts of dodging away.  there is also no air combat(jumping falling etc.) (despite there bieng an air combat statistic its only for when you are on the ground...)

other things.  there are allot of profesions to occupie your time with but only a few that have anything to do with regular play.  training helps your horsies level faster, cooking is obvious plus eating things increases bonus health exp, alchemy also obvious potions, production for making things you can't afford to buy off market because there is no trading.  and the company actualy embraces afk leveling.  the nodes are mostly for workers grinding away at materials needed for profs and end game item farming.

One big aspect of this game being a great time is that you have all the makings for a story of your own. Yep, role-playing. Not using shortcuts, taking everything off the UI on screen, already you'll find the game more interesting. Now, decide to only play as realistically as you would if you were there. You wouldn't stand in the middle of their camp and hope to shoot them all first. I get the Owl out, recce ahead, plan my moves two or three ahead. I find the outter enemies of an encampment or whatever the best to pick off first, just as I would in real life. I summon my stealthest beast.   The stragglers get eaten without out any alarms.   You know what Im getting at. This game is a fantastic open canvas of how ever you like to play. I was about to refund this game, but I decided to try realistic style approach.  No helps, no exploits, no cheesy running in and taking your chances. You wouldn't do that in real life. But in this game does it ever bring in the suspension of disbelief.
Give it a good try. The game becomes all that you wished it would do for you. But this is a game you play close to the bone, and it comes alive. I'm 24% through, and 30 hours into it. I have 3/4 of a game left, and I'm already not wanting it to end.  There is just so much you can do in this game, but it will take a choice on your part. Are you willing to put a bit of effort into it, or moan, because the Dev's have left something out that you feel makes the game poor.  Not a chance, This is a polished, smooth running, innovative aspects of stealth, pet taming, etc. Brilliant. Can't wait to see where this goes.
Developer's, thanks you for a wonderful labour of love youve put into your game. The details prove that over and over, that this game shines, and its ready for prime-time gameplay, for me anyway.
Of course, ymmv.  But give it a good shot, before you give up on it.

Lost Castle is pretty much Castle Crashers meets Binding of Isaac. If that sounds appealing, then you should consider picking this up. It's cheap and addicting, but also kind of hard, and offers plenty of replayability.
There are plenty of items to unlock and find, which skews gameplay toward that "Insane Collection of Powerups" feel that Isaac fans are familiar with. There is a lot of variety in the items, including the weapon and armour types, but the game seems more punishing for melee types. Lots of the bigger baddies have no hitstun from melee, which means you will take a ton of damage from them. Hit & run tactics are not always feasible because the enemies are often quicker than you, so you will just be hit anyway, and getting hit is terrible in this game, where you have very limited health ups and permadeath. Not sure what I'd suggest to improve that balance. Maybe it's just a playstyle thing.
The one big change I would want to see is the ability to backtrack within one of the 5 stages.
And more items that do zany things.

A Fistful of Gun is a fast-paced, kinetic top down shooter with an over-the-top spaghetti western aesthetic and bullet hell influences. AFOG features a single player and local co op story mode and mutliplayer versus and arcade modes.
PROS:
+Amazing soundtrack
+Juicy as hell, shooting, moving and dodging all feel great. Big, slow moving bullets
+Extremely fast paced, you'll rarely spend more than 30 seconds on a screen
+up to 9 player co op + local co op
+11 characters each with their own shooting style, control scheme and advantages/disadvantages
+Gorgeous visuals
CONS
-Long (3-5 second) loading screens between areas can break up the adrenaline and franticness of the gameplay
-Quiet online servers, but this isn't a problem if you play with friends.
Definitely recommended for anyone who likes top down shooters, bullet hell, and co-op.

The game is simple, you either devise a strategy or work with your team towards the goal of destrying the enemy base while making sure yours survives. Mines, traps, turrets, devices, gismos... uses them to your advantage. It makes no sense to lose a match with a full pool of resources.
Same with ammo, shoot them up, don't run away when the enemies, SHOOT! You can always walk backwards towards cover while shooting the enemies, giving you a chance to kill them instead them kill you.
Never charge the base alone (unless you are a distraction to lure enemies away or you are on a sabatauge run). Same can be applied to defending the base. NEVER leave your base undefended. Someone has to bite the bullet and stay behind. I would recommend two stay at the base, though that's asking for alot out of gun-ho players. (Like most of you are.
The field can easily be divided into three sections (five zones) which is yoiur base, their base, and the battlement in between (or on bigger maps, you have to add the outpost cubes for your side and their side). Above all, protect your base with traps and defenders in a way that your raid party will have time to wreck the enemy.
[The following is based on my suggestion. If you want, skip it and move to the following section (or if you are that impatient, move to a comment that is shorter and easier for your miniturized brain to comprehend. These next sections are for those who give a care and will be useful in a match.]
So here is the suggestion section -- dig your trenches early in. If you have an explosive like rockets, grenades, or anything that does great damage to blocks in a short time, use it sparingly on the terrain to weaken it. Digging a trench makes does a fe things: makes it harder for the enemies to get past it without the likelihood of being seen (depending on how deep and wide it is) makes it harder to get across then a flat surface, and you also can get resources you harvest with your dig tool. Dig smart with the tool. Carving out a chunk of blocks then letting the rest fall will not only speed up the digging but also give you more resourse then you had to actually dig for. You can always build a bulwark (shaped like a stairway) to which you can get across yet the enemy can't (it also doubles as protection)
Also, be creative with trap placement, nothing works better to killing your foes then a bomb that they didn't suspect.
Alright, last section. Think of this as a "either do this or fail" list of do and don't.
DO: Kill the enemies. Since there is little time for party, focus on killing those who are NOT on your team.
DON'T:Wreck your ally traps. As much of a pain for them placing things in the way, do not break them, most will harm/kill you if you do and it does cost resources to place, don't go douching... go to Minecraft for that.
DO: Wreck enemy traps if you see them, better take them out before they take out one of your own.
DON'T: ...simply destroy enemy spawners or teleporters. Be creative, layer it in mines so the next enemy to come through it will have a rude pre-mature death. HAH!!!
DO: Stay in the battlements if you like killing players, you can best defend your allies if you're killing the enemies.
DON'T: Leave your base unguarded, EVER! All it takes is a sense of your team winning to ignore your base long enough for them to get inside and destry your chance at winning. Sure there's next time, though if a match drags on, you better win it!
DO: Make it miserable for the enemies to get to your base. Radar, traps, and chokeholds will make it a nightmare for them to get an easy win.
DON'T: ...cover the cube. Don't even think about it. If it's covered, and the enemies gets in, then you have to dig them out. Turrets and traps will do better at keeping them out, and if you must have walls , build them a bit back from the cube, place traps on it or use it to slow them down.
DO: Realise that NOTHING can KEEP the ENEMIES completely OUT of you BASE guarunteedly FOREVER!!! Take as much time as needed to set up your defenses but realise: every second you delay is another second the enemies are crawling their way to winning.
DON'T: ...waste time. Makes sure that you make your moments count. Your player's death is inevitable as long as you are outside the base's spawn. If you are afaid to die, then you are playing the wrong game. ...just realise that it takes time to respawn. So if you're going to die, make it where you bide enough time so you can get back in the action without missing a beat.
And above all... DO: make use of the Recall option. If a unit makes a pit trap and you fall in it, don't go wrecking it, use Recall to escape. It takes a bit of time, though it takes less time to use it then to repair damage to the trap.
Alright, if I can edit this later, I will. Though this is more then enough to know what to do.

===
Solstice Chronicles: MIA is a top down shooter set in a future where mega-corporations have gained a great deal of power. You will impersonate one of the numerous grunts these corporation have on their payroll; left abadoned in a facility after a terrbile plague, you will have to find a way past all the hordes of mutated people and creatures and make it back alive. The premises sound simple, but this game has surprising variety and content, as you will soon read about.
===
The gameplay of Solstice Chronicles: MIA is the typical one expected from a top-down shooter, and inspires to some all-time classics of the genre such as Alien Shooter or Alien Swarm. This at the core, but the developers have also tried to introduce new mechanics and innovate to keep the formula fresh: such new mechanics are, for example, passive and active abilities to unlock as you progress through the levels, a useful companion drone which has 4 unique skills, a Threat Level that manages spawn rate and strenght of enemies in levels and can be modified by using certain skills, Stamina management and supply points management. All these new non-classic mechanics help this game to be up-to-date with 2017 standards. basically you will have to run through endlessly spawning enemies from every side, completing different objectives and reaching the end of the level alive. You will have 3 lives each level, if dawned you will be able to ressurect, but each time with less HP. Health regens over-time or with medkits, there are 4 classes and each has its own skill tree and abilities.
Combat is fast-paced, full of gore, meaty, and substantial. Great hordes of enemies will swarm you, and composed from beasts ranging from small and fast to huge and dangerous. There are however some helping features to aid you in your battle: first is the target selector, a consumable that can be used with almost any weapon, that will allow you to aim automatically and score critical hits until you run out of battery, which won't take long, then there is your drone, which has 4 skills: Scout, Bomb, Block and Taunt, each has a different use and is powerful in its own way, for example Bomb deploys a field that damages all enemies when triggered, but the bigger it gets the less damage it does, so it's up to you to decide the right moment, instead Taunt prompts all enemies in the level at that time to chase you, useful to set up ambushes. There is quite a tactical component to combat especially at higher difficulties, enemies will be dangerous and won't forgive many mistakes.
The campaign has a substantial amount of levels, and also Survival endless mode is present. If you want to play the whole campaign with all the four classes, it will take tou quite some time. As far as weapons, skills and equiment goes, there is plenty in this game, between standard ones, special ones, class skills, general skills, consumables etc. With aalso local co op, shame it's not online, real shame, supporting 2 players, you will have a lot on your hands for this price range.
At higher difficulties the enemy will definitely have the upper hand unless you have a good strategy and stamina management, few mistakes will be fatal and using skills and drone powers correctly will be a must. Generally the game is difficult as it should be at maximum difficulty, but is also fair enough. Some weapons are a bit OP like the flamer which has infinte ammo and can shoot through WALLS (!) but generally we are on good levels as far as belance is concerned.
Highest difficulty is really tough if you are for this kind of things, don't know about MERC difficulty which possibly is unlocked only after completing the game, i suppose it's even tougher.
===
Game runs on unreal engine... 3 i think, graphics are decent but a bit dated in some thigns like textures and effects. It's not exactly top notch in this, even if artwork and lighting are good. Generally the graphics do the job, but are only decent, not more than that. Models and meshes are detailed enough, cutscenes though highlight all the lack of detail that is a consequence of using a 10 year old engine.
Sound effects and soundtrack are decent, they do the job but nothing good, or bad, is to be said.
Even with high end hardware, ins oem cases drops to 15-20 fps have been registered with no reason, though not often. Optimization problems are there but do not affect the game very seriously.
No crashes or errors found.
Basic follow-and-attack enemy AI, nothing more or less, typical of this kind of games, no special mentions to be done.
Controls and UIs do the job, both with mouse/keyboard and gamepad the game controls are responsive and well made, key rebind is possible anyway.
Apart from the flamer being able to shoot through walls, didn't notice any other bugs worth mentioning.
===
6.5 / 10
A decent top down survival shooter with some new mechanics that keep it fresh and up to date with the times, still the lack of online co op, performance problems and using a dated engine bring this title down quite a bit. I suggest purchasing if you want a good shooter to play on your own or maybe some family member in split screen, for this price range it's not too bad.

This is the first (and so far, only) XCOM game I've played, so I can't compare it to any of the previous games.
Originally acquired this game a couple years back when it was a free download for "PS Plus" members. Saw the PC version on sale at Gamestop a few weeks back for $11, so I quickly picked up the PC version. This is a Tactical FPS (TFPS?). Each "battle" takes place on a map that's similar to the ones used in TRPG's like Final Fantasy Tactics. And like RPG's, you can level up your guys (by increasing their rank - Sergeant, Lieutenant, etc.) to give them improved skills, like increasing the effectiveness of using Med Packs, or giving Snipers a bonus to their Aim if they're shooting at someone that's at a lower elevation.
Your home base is where you'll spend your time when you're not out hunting down aliens. It's a 4-level building, built below ground. You'll start out with only a couple buildings on the first level. You'll have to pay to excavate the rest of your home base, as well as pay for whatever buildings you decide to build.
Even if you play the game on the easiest mode, this game will still prove to be a little bit of a challenge w/o using cheats.  Which is one thing I liked. It's not "we'll let you walk all over us back and forth" easy, but it wasn't "We can 2-shot you blindfolded from a mile away" difficult.

SOLSTICE CHRONICLES: MIA (--ALPHA VERSION/May 2017--)
PUBLISHER – Ironward
DEVELOPER – Ironward
GENRE – Indie, Action, Twin-stick Shooter, RPG-ish, Rogue-lite (in Survival)
THE BASICS: Note – Playable Alpha version.
THE FLOW AND THE STORY:
A mining accident has taken place on Mars; little else is shown in-game. Plenty of nasty creatures have since infested the area. You and your sentient AI drone have to pick up the pieces, find out what happened to the miners, and clean house. You'll pick up new weapons along the way, such as Gauss guns, shotguns, and flamethrowers for your power-armor suited Marine to wield (two main weapons at any time, plus one “disposable” weapon that cannot be reloaded). You'll also find various special items such as turrets, grenades, and super ammo packs to help liven up the party.
Your drone friend, Saffron, can also take advantage of a few special abilities of its own – setting a huge bomb that takes time to go off (better run!), bringing you supply drops at the cost of increasing the Threat level (enemy strength/numbers), and the like.
Survival mode is also available, where you have to manage limited resources against increasingly powerful waves of bad guys, constantly moving and discovering new areas so that you can gather much-needed ammo and gear. Feeling overwhelmed? Go for an Evac point. Escape, and you can permanently carry your upgrades forward for future attempts; die on the battlefield, and you lose everything you were carrying. Local co-op Multiplayer is also available in this mode.
CONTROLS:
XBONE controller seems to work well, tho menus benefit from using the mouse. Modified twin-stick style. Left stick to move (press to sprint); right stick to aim (press to auto-lockon); right trigger to fire. Other triggers/bumpers use specific special items. Single-shot weapons use precision aiming via a laser sight; spray-n-pray ones like the shotgun show a spread of possible impact points. You can also pick up and toss barrels that make a satisfying BOOM when they land.
GRAPHICS:
Dark, gritty, Alien-esque. Could use a little cleanup and more variety, but that will come in time.
SOUND:
Solid sounds, good atmosphere; little to no music is present as of the Alpha.
OVERALL:
This has potential to be a great game. There just needs to be more of it! They had a successful crowdfunding campaign on Fig.
SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS:
Requires Windows 7 or later.

Telltale's bigger failure so far.
This was a gigantic disappointment. With The Walking Dead or The Wolf Among Us, Telltale nailed the feel, the narrative and the general tone of the original works. Not this time though, as they completely misunderstood what made the books (and TV series I guess) good or enjoyable, thinking that unfairness, frustration and characters dying and having the worst outcome in every situation is what makes GoT fun. You cannot succeed, you cannot win and no matter how cunning, how tough, how smart or how remarkably stupid you act, the outcome is ALWAYS going to be the same. This game goes as far as to have major plot twists happen in the exact same manner even if the characters that are supposed to carry that out are dead, just having someone else do it instead.
As far as the characters go, the game attempts to retake the book's formula of having the story told from every character's perspective, and it would've worked amazingly if the characters weren't either a rip off or a mix between the original Stark family. I mean, really, they even look alike.  The villains and secondaries aren't much better though, when Telltale thinks "unpredictable" is the same as "incoherent", and no matter how good you are in figuring them out, they'll just act randomly and have the plot continue.
Gameplay is pretty much non-existent, even for Telltale's standards. This game focuses heavily in dialogue, choices and interactions between characters, leaving exploration and investigation somewhat behind, and the usual QT events for the action parts. However good the intentions were, when psychology, diplomacy, bluffs, etc. are the only tools you have, but the story will NEVER branch into different outcomes... well, you can guess.
And that's the worst part by far. When you have almost no gameplay and a heavy plot with several wannabe cliffhangers and plot twists, the player needs to feel involved. For the most part, Telltale's GoT feels as if you were reading a poorly written fanfic of the original books with the characters acting in your screen. As a player, you have ZERO power over the events. Dialogue hardly ever changes, as you're going to be completely screwed up anyway.
If you play this game, get ready to have a pretty big cast of characters tell you it was your decisions that led the entire plot into a complete bloodshed, disaster and chaos no matter what you choose to do.
On a side note, though the animations are pretty crappy overall, general art work, environment and assets are pretty damn good. It is a rather pretty game, visually, I'll give em that.
I'd say don't pour a single cent into this mess of a story, I expected Telltale to get better at this, not worse, and this game is below mediocre.

The Hyperdimension Neptunia franchise is an ongoing series of JRPG games that serve as a parody of all the abundant tropes in these type of games, in the way that Ouron High School Host Club is a shojo, but also parodies shojo tropes. Everything about this game is fantastic, as it likes to deceptively market itself as every other banal and generic anime title like the thousands of others we are barraged with on the Steam marketplace. The dialogue, story and characters are all very charming and memorable, with loads of legitimately hilarious moments and witty back and forth banter, as well as loads of fourth wall-breaking dialogue and references to other anime such as JoJo and Fullmetal Alchemist, two of my personal favorites. My favorite character would most definitely be the main character Neptune or Nep for short, her constant mockery of annoying JRPG tropes like characters who have amnesia or various Deus Ex Machina elements, were hilarious to read. It's almost as if it's a gigantic middle finger to all the insufferable modern final fantasy games and how they have completely destroyed the genre. Combat is fun and intuitive and can easily be picked up and played by anyone, but also provides a fair amount of difficulty, it's essentially a mix of turn based combat and button mashing various combos, which is a blast and never feels stale at all. There is a fair amount of grinding involved for later chapters and boss fights, but it never once felt like a chore, in fact, during a weekend I had logged over 20 hours on the game, which gives you an idea of just how entertaining it can be. The environments are designed well enough, but I would be lying if I said it wasn't occasionally linear in the dungeon designs and they even re-hash certain areas despite the game not even being that big to begin with. But regardless, I enjoyed constantly leveling up my characters, getting badass new equipment and searching for hidden items, in fact, I was able to max out nearly every character in the game, and with it's multiple endings and new character unlocks, it provides the player with even more hours of gameplay and replay-ability. Overall, this game is the ♥♥♥♥♥♥s and is a much needed breath of fresh air in a Japanese industry constantly throwing out game after game of the same CGI-laden melodrama we've been treated to for far too long. I damn well am looking forward to delving into the several other available games in the franchise.

I originally rated this game negatively based on the fact it is essentially an inferior version of mk2, and I stand by this opinion. The dialogue is worse--they rewrote and rerecorded all of it, and it is generally a lot less funny. Red and Broccoli aren't nearly as entertaining as Nisa and Gust, either. I don't know why they did this, considering the story and events are otherwise identical. Maybe legal issues required changing Nisa and Gust, but there was no reason to butcher a superior script.
I guess after playing Re;Birth 1, I was expecting a new game instead of mk2 again. Re;Birth 1 was a complete overhaul of the first Neptunia game, and really, nothing like it--thank goodness. I thought Re;Birth 2 was going to be similarly fresh, rather than ruining my memory of mk2. I don't have a Vita and never looked into what was happening with the series on it. Maybe more informed fans already knew what the deal was with Re;Birth 2 and 3. It wasn't until I played Re;Birth 3 on PC that I realized what was going on, so I decided to update this review.
To make a long story short, I reconsidered my negative rating as not really being fair to the game for what it is rather than what I expected it to be. It's still decent and worth playing, especially if you didn't catch mk2 on the PS3.
----------Original Negative Review Below-------------------------------------------
I don't really get what they were trying to do with this game. It follows the same plot pattern as Hyperdimension Neptunia mk2 for the PS3, except worse characters, worse dialogue, worse jokes, worse everything, story-wise. It seems like a rough-draft for mk2. I would accuse them of being cheap, but then they re-recorded all the voice acting to match the new dialogue, which seems to contradict the assumption they were just being cheap. If they were, it would have been just a direct port as far as story and dialogue. Maybe they had some kind of legal issues.
As far as game play, it's identical to re;birth1. The only addition is a runs-in-the-background minigame that can score you some unique treasure, but is very simplistic and minimally interactive--it's basically just a timer you let run down while you are doing other things. The dungeon/monster change plans get carried over from re;birth1, as does the build-your-own disc thing and the finishing moves. These weren't in mk2, so the game play is slightly evolved to make up for the worse story.
I think the music is the same, except for a worse (that word keeps coming up) opening movie theme. Mostly the same voice actors as mk2, but they re-recorded the dialogue, as mentioned before. They did add repetitive idle chatter on the world map that is almost as annoying as listening to drivers laying on their horns in GTA.
Graphics, textures, models, and dungeons are essentially the same as mk2. You can select the resolution, though, so it will look a little better. I haven't had any crashes or issues, so it's a decent port, at least.
If you have played mk2, you'll probably be disappointed in re;birth2. I loved mk2, and was thoroughly disappointed. If you haven't played mk2 but like re;birth1, it's essentially more of the same, so if that's what you're looking for, get it. If you are bored of re;birth1, you'll be bored of this. If you haven't played either, buy it. It's marginally better than re;birth1 and a decent place to start with Neptunia.
I was kind of annoyed at how they butchered mk2's story and wanted to give a thumbs down, but I don't know why I bothered to write a review. It seems like the only thing Steam reviews are for is witty one-liners and 11/10-would-screw again's, so if you read all this, congratulations.

+ Open world Farcry 3/4 'reskin' with new location/items etc

+ Crafting system
+ Addition of beasts

Overall, like most games nowadays unless you're a huge fan of the franchise I don't see it being worth full price. If you liked Farcry 3 or 4, wait until it is on sale and grab it for 30-50% off and enjoy 30+hrs in the world.
