Now THIS is how you make an ARPG!
Played Titan Quest back in the day, enjoyed it. Seeing people involved with that project doing this was definitely a selling point.
I really like many of the game's features...Seems every time I do another playthrough, I find other aspects of the game I previously didn't know exist. This keeps the game fresh and shows that an ARPG can have more depth than people give them credit for.
The levelling system is awesome. Instead of picking your class at the beginning of the game, you do this once you've gained a level. There are six masteries to choose from. Once you reach level 10, you can add a second mastery and the title changes accordingly  (Soldier + nighblade = blademaster, Shaman + occultist = conjurer, etc.). With the skill trees available to you, even a second playthrough at the same class can be a completely different experience.
The world setting is a combination of classic medieval RPG's with some steampunk elements. The Devs put a lot of time into creating the world and its lore. Lots of notes and journals can be found throughout the game fleshing out the history. You can also have conversations with people who will give you background on the world.
Augmenting all of this are crafting items and components. Components can be added to items. They do such things as help with resistances, add damage, increase attack speed and even give new abilities.
As if this wasn't enough the game has a devotion system. When you earn devotion points by cleansing/restoring shrines, you use a "constellation" system to select new abilities and augments. This is more refined than it may sound, as there are paths that need to be taken to achieve the more powerful constellations.
Excellent replayability, fascinating classes, crafting done well, and killing tons of monsters. Did I leave anything out? Oh yes...They're adding two new masteries and 10 more constellations in an expansion, AND raising the level cap.
If you love ARPG's, BUY THIS GAME. You won't be dissapointed!

Grim Dawn is a Hack and Slash ARPG Dungeon crawler developed by Crate Entertainment and released Feb 25, 2016.
You play as the "Taken", a humanoid who was possessed by an Etherial being but sparred because right before the host was killed the Ethereal left your body and you were then saved from the hangman's noose.
The rest of the game will be navigating this apocalyptic world, helping it's few survivors, and blowing the crap out of anything with a health bar or ambient object, like a chair or vase.
I'll be the first to admit to you that I feel very unqualified to talk in depth about ARPG's and dungeon crawlers. I'm a simple man who makes simple choices when it comes to this Genre.
You start out with a character male or female, play online, co op, or by yourself, as you progress you pick up random junk and kill the undead with it.
After you level up a couple times you can choose between six classes, after a while you can even select a duel class, but I didn't do that because I put all my points into one class.
Grim Dawn is a looooonggggg game, you can take this one of two ways: 1) "Oh crap, I need to spend 30+ hours to beat the game, well crap, I guess I don't have the time for that". 2) "Challenge accepted".
I think you can guess what my choice was.
Grim Dawn Delivers what many people wanted out of it. What with Torchlight 2, Path of Exile, Diablo, and Grim dawn, there are plenty of games in the genre to keep someone very busy indeed.

Lethal League is one of the most intense dodgeball type games I've seen in my life. Maybe even THE most intense. This game makes it so the ball goes really fast. And I mean FAST. The maximum speed a ball can get to is 10,000. That is ridiculous. The characters are all very enjoyable too. The aim is to get the most points or be the last one standing. When you hit someone with the ball, they go flying across the screen and off it. The characters play pretty much the same, but with different special moves. Raptor's baseball bat can send the ball going straight forward, Switch's kick flip can make the ball move weirdly and confuse players, Candyman can confuse the player by sending the ball across the screen and looping to the other side of it, Sonata's bass drop can give the ball extra speed, Latch can eat the ball and spit it out whenever he wants, and Dice's curve shot can send the ball flying in weird angles. If the ball gets enough speed, the stage can noticeably change. That's kind of a tough to notice detail, but it's cool.
Overall it's a crazy dodgeball fighting game. The ball goes everywhere, crazy attacks can be performed, and people go flying off the screen. That's why my final rating for this game is a Super Smash Bros. out of 10. (Want a real rating? 8 out of 10.)

Dying Light is the third edition to Techlands Zombie Killing games, and manages to incorporate some familiar, and improved features from Dead Island 1 and Riptide, with a few weak points here and there.
You have your weapon crafting and repairing system, similar to how Dead Island Riptide handled it, but this time, you're able to have increased stats from weapon mods which effect how much damage your weapon does, or even the speed and critical rate, which is nice to have once you learn how it works.
Weapon Quantity has been increased too, with more unique variants of weapons, and base weapons when compared to Dead Island or even Riptide, with the rest being DLC weapons that have their models and textures locked away until you purchase the dlc, which isn't bad, but the Bozak Horde DLC is a bit questionable, but we'll get to that later.
The graphics and animation are a major step up from Dead Island 1 & Riptide, with more fluid animations, more animations in general, and proper god rays and beautiful textures that are nice to look at.
Low-Tier gaming rigs should avoid playing the game on ultra, anything with, let's say a 550ti can run the game on high settings or more.
The weakest point of the game, cardboard box tier character interest, and an annoying QTA sequence that'll happen to you makes it a bit frustrating to get through, there's some interesting characters here and there, just not enough of them.
One of the earliest DLC's done with Dying Light, you're able to be invaded by Night Hunters controlled by other players, or do it yourself!
You can turn this off or have certain conditions before it happens, It's pretty fun and hilarious to surprise friends with.
Mostly used for its weapons, The Bozak Horde offers a short story alone or with your friends, with the story being mostly forgettable, and the final boss being poorly implemented.
The Following offers and entirely new world, rivaling that of the main game itself, with places to explore, side quests to do, and an all new
to ride in, so you can mow zombies over and get to places faster.
Sadly, It's exclusive to the DLC Worldspace, but the main game is cramped enough and meant for parkour so it's reasonable.
Dying Light is a pretty decent zombie killing game, one of the underrated games that came out in 2015, It's fun alone, and even more enjoyable with friends.

Definitely feels like an early release and I'd feel better about recommending it if it was labeled as such.  While the game does offer some fun to be had it feels pretty unpolished and has some annoying elements.  Namely that you have to complete 5 levels for every class just to see their skill trees and abilities.  Once you do the limitations of customization become readily apparent, with each class you can only use one of the three native abilities at any given time and you can not expermient with them untill points are invested, the exception is the demolition class which can slot all three native abilities but is also the only class that gains consumable slots for non-native abilities so if you do decide to use all native abilities your other passive bonus is useless.  There are many little poor design choices.  The best weapon in the game is only available to the most tanky class, the hellfire class flamethrower making it the clearly the best class in the game imo.  The standard game weapons are for the most part a bit lackluster and the soldier is the only class that gets a bonus to the standard weapons with a dmg increase during sustained fire.
The tutorials and threat meter mechanic never really come together in any meaningful way.  Most of the levels end really abruptly, sometimes just getting close to an exit while the screen is still filled with enemies you intend to keep fighting will suddenly trigger the end of the mission.  There are absolutely no bonuses to killing more enemies or stronger elite enemies, at the end of levels you get the same number of skill points to allot and no level specific suit or weapon upgrades carry beyond the level you are on.
Survival mode actually brings together the games elements together in a more cohesive way than the campaign does but with only one map and identical objectives everytime it becomes monotonous pretty quickly.
I hope the developers keep working on this game to make it feel like a more coherent and fleshed out game as it does have some decent elements but I can't reccomend paying full or close to full price in the games present condition.

Having loved CoH the first version I thought I would take advantage of the free play weekend.
As many others may have done, we have eagerly awaited a sequel to what in many people’s minds was, and still is a brilliant game. Brilliant, I thought, I can try for CoH2 for free. Oddly I was reminded of the days of old when we would buy a PC magazine with a CD attached, we  could go home and install it, play the game demo, and away you go you would either want more or you would leave it. Anyway, I digress.
I downloaded the game etc etc. Clicked start and was immediately struck by the superficiality and lack of real depth. We are hit with a simple cinematic (perhaps this is a stripped Steam version I may need correction here) and bang we are in, no real atmosphere or scene was set in contrast to the quasi story personalised as in the original CoH. To immerse yourself fully you have to have some prior knowledge of this conflict to really appreciate the fundamental change in tactic that goes hand in hand that is required by the player to understand this expansion. In sum sacrifice is the mode of the day.  As another reviewer aptly summarises; the days of CoH allowing for an individual approach to gameplay such as defend, or inch by inch ground gains are gone in this release, hence the flavour of individual gameplay so loved in the original is overbearingly crushed by the mechanics of this expansion. Whilst trying to capture the spirit of expendability synonymous with the military approach of the time, little consideration was (supposedly) given to impact this may have on gameplay when transposing this approach to a RTS platform.
However, at $16.99 on steam free play weekend you would think it would be a steal, considering the relative time between its release and now right? Wrong, very wrong. Please do not get caught by this as it is as close to a legal scam as you will get. Yes, I mean DLC, and there is lots of it.
I'm sorry, even at the budget price of $17 there is no way I am touching this game, even with the deep affection I have for the first one. I really feel Sega and Relic are hoping to cash in on an emotional attachment that many of us have for the first game. One reviewer mentioned a bait and switch scam, which I have to agree with as that is what I might feel caught by if I buy into this DLC horror.
To this very day, I play hours of this game. If you by chance came across this review and havent purchased the game yet, do it. It is worth every second.

They took a very big gamble making a game like this, and trying to focus their assets more on the story, than they would on multiplayer survival, like their previous entry into the solstice universe. The story is just kind of "meh". It is generic to the point its forgetable. The real meat of the game does come from MIA's survival mode.
The gameplay is easy enough, its a twin stick shooter. The only complaint I really have is that grenades are launched in the direction my character is facing, instead of where my mouse is pointing. So while running I will throw a grenade right on top of myself. Its a horde based survival game, you are going to keep moving. Throwing a nade in front of you, as you are required to keep moving is a very terrible idea and a very big design flaw.
The remedy for this would be to have the feet and torso work on separate axis. The torso moves around via the mouse, while the legs move via wsad. As its set up, the torso and legs move with wsad and the gun moves with mouse. You can aim behind and start firing, which will slowly move your characters torso towards the mouse, but that will only burn ammo. Instead you have to turn and face 100 enemies, right on your tail, to fire at them, or use abilities.
Survival is quite enjoyable. However making a horde mode, objective style game, does not work without multiplayer. Due to local coop only, it has severely limited replayability. A good game is supposed to make you feel like you are progressing, and that this progression has made a difference. This game succeeds at the former, but severely fails at the latter. Sure I know I've done something amazing, but no one else does, due to the fact my character is all alone.
I am sorry but my recommendation is no, at this time. It is a risky gamble to focus on what they did, and I do not feel it paid off. Their previous entry is incredibly fun if you like a commando style, rts, survival game. The community on it is mostly dead, but if you can get enough of your friends to play, its a blast. I would recommend you look into The Red Solstice instead of this.
Note: I do have some fun with Solstice Chronicles: MIA, I just wont recommend it at this time. Wait for a sale or grab it if they add online multiplayer, which they said they would "only add if the sales do well, due to a limited budget"... Generic story devs... generic...

I think Solstice Chronicles is a well-made game, but I think this review could have been done better by someone who can appreciate its gameplay more than me. I got excited for the game when I saw the trailer and imagined that I would be firing a lot of bullets, massacring a plethora of monsters, and fast-paced movement. Unfortunately, ammo conservation is a bigger issue than I'd like and the movement is very slow, even taking into account abilities and sprinting. While it could be argued that both of these aspects  add to the challenge of the game, they feel like challenges that aren't fun to work with.
However, it’s impossible for me to ignore the work that was put into this game. Features like the threat system and the varied skill trees add depth to the gameplay, and allows for the freedom to try many different playstyles. Even with the help of the tutorial and a full understanding of the game’s mechanics, each level makes you feel as if you hit the ground running. A strategy that works once may not always work again, and adaptation to constant change and waves of monsters is essential - and I only played on the second easiest difficulty. Besides that, the animations, graphics, and sound effects give the impression of a game that has had a lot of work put into it.
In conclusion, take my own impression of the game with a grain of salt. Just because it’s not the game for me, doesn’t mean it’s not the game for you. If you like the way the game looks, and if you like using a combination of weapons and abilities to defeat a larger or stronger force using your wit, then this is probably the game for you. It's not the fast-paced shooter I was hoping for, but I only have my poor researching abilities to blame for that.
PROS
+ Variety of playstyles are encouraged
+ Graphically impressive environment
+ Sound effects are on point
CONS
- Movement is slow, even with abilities
- Constant need to conserve ammo is annoying

My previous review had been negative (comments on the review were from before I switched to a positive attitude about the game just FYI). However, devs contacted me (whaaat? Devs? Contact such mere players? I have hope for this game), and assured me that several of the issues I noted would be fixed. And they did not disappoint.
PROS:
-Many annoying glitches/bugs have been fixed. This has made the game much more enjoyable to play (obviously).
-Fairly regular updates. New areas, monsters, bosses, and improvements to English text were made last update, and constant bug fixes happen. To me, this is very good.
-Boss diversity. This was a HUGE plus for me. None of the bosses are really the same. Some of them may have similar fighting styles, but their techniques and attacks are all different. It takes actual strategy to beat these buggers.
-Art style. This may seem miniscule, but I really enjoy the art to this game. It just makes it all the more enjoyable in the long run.
-Grinding has been reduced. Oh, praise the sun! Grinding in any game gets boring and repetitive. Lost Castle has done a good job of minimizing grind, and maximizing fun. Good on ya devs!
CONS:
-Game can get a little repetitive. Not a super huge issue, as the devs have done really well in randomizing rooms, so you don't really notice it a whole lot. And each room is generally packed with different stuff to keep it interesting.
-Nightmare mode is HARD. Past the point of being challenging (for me anyway) and just into the realm of somewhat frustrating.I have a lvl 70ish character, and I still can't run nightmare mode all that well. Of course, I might just suck at the game. That's entirely possible XD But they weren't kidding about calling it "Nightmare" mode.
Overall, I think these devs have definitely done a splendid job in cutting bugs and glitches, and resolving text/grind problems. Lost Castle has become a rather enjoyable game. Playing it with my little bro is fun, except he doesn't really get the concept of a roguelike just yet XD
I'd rate it an 8/10 not perfect, but very enjoyable.

'Game of Thrones' is in my opinion is a solid game from Telltale. I enjoyed 'The Walking Dead' and 'A Wolf Among Us' more but as a fan of both the books and the show that this is based on I think it's a worthwhile addition to the saga.
I'll preface this review with a few notes:
1. Unlike Telltale's 'The Walking Dead' and 'A Wolf Among Us', 'Game of Thrones' expects you to be familiar with the world it's based on. The game starts with the expectation that you will know who the different characters are and how they go along with each other. Furthermore, if you aren't caught up with 'Game of Thrones' through at least the first few episodes of Season 4 (or the first three books), you probably shouldn't play this. You will get spoiled on quite a few major events.
2. This is a Telltale game. If this is your first one, they basically function as interactive movies where your character(s)'s choices will impact what happens. A common criticism is that 90% of the story will play out the same regardless of what you do but at the same time they're well-made stories so it depends on what you're looking for.
The game follows House Forrester, a small Northern family loyal to House Stark. In light of recent events in the war, their situation is dire and they must play the game of thrones to survive. True to the original series, the game follows several different characters across Westeros; one member of the family is handmaiden to Margaery Tyrell, another is exiled to Essos. Much of the choices the player makes involves either doing the morally right thing or advancing one's cause; should you betray a friend if it means you get a higher station?
The story is a strong one and I actually enjoyed it more than I did the fifth season of the show. There are varied characters and most of them are interesting with their own motivations. At the same time, the abundance of characters made it more difficult for me to care about all of them the same way I cared about Lee or Clementine over at TWD. Another issue I had was that many of the characters are in effect proxies of the Starks from the main series, fulfilling similar roles so there's a sense of deja vu.
Back to the criticism that "your choices don't matter"; well it's true and it's not true. On one hand, there is a mostly linear plot that your characters will follow. On another, I felt that the player had greater impact on the story than some of the other Telltale games. Depending on how you play it there are certain characters who will live or die by your decisions and various characters will find themselves in different situations by the game's end as a result of your choices.
Finally, some have said that the story is grim. I suppose, but this IS 'Game of Thrones'. That's all I'll say in that regard.
So what it boils down to is this: we have a strong story, interesting if at times familiar characters, and some degree of decision as to how the story unfolds. If you're a fan of Telltale's style and 'Game of Thrones' then I would recommend this.

Basic review and opinion: Amamzing game, with clever and fast paced action keeping you on your toes at all times during the game. As well the amount of ships and layouts to unlock make it so that you have so much to keep playing for. Personally I have put many hours into trying to get a single ship, and the payout is glorious when you finally do it. 8/10 Highly Recommended.
Frustration level: To say that this game is frustrating at times is a very large understatement, as at times it has made me want to throw my laptop across the room. This game is very rage inducing, but not because of something that IT did, most, if not all rage and frustration are from player mistakes. Yes it was a missle that killed you, but it was your fault for not repairing your ship in a shop. This game will force feed you humble pie, as you will begin to realize that it was not RNG or Bad luck that got you killed, but your own mistakes.
Gameplay (Mostly the combat and first impressions of mine): This game will look very bland and slow paced from a viewers perspective, having to wait for lasers to fire and watching as they only take a small block of health from the enemy each shot. However from a players POV the game is much faster paced, as not only do you have to keep track of so many systems and crew, but you also will have to send crew all around the ship to repair and activate weapons/shields/etc. The game takes a little while to get into, as for veteran players will feel bored with the beginning grind in the first sectors, while new players will feel like they are drowning in things they have to memorize and do. However once you reach about sector 4 or 5 the game picks up drastically, as the real race begins: Your ship is now running out of the fuel you had in the beginning and you are running into battles with much tougher ships, and you feel as though your next jump could be your last with every click of the mouse. This caught me by surprise my first playthrough, and I got horribly murdered by a massive enemy, and I sat back in my chair wondering what the heck happened. The other large part of the game is the Risk/Reward evaluation that you have to do at every choice. Some are obvious, turn over a crew member or attack the ship. But ones like the giant space spider station will always have random results, sometimes you get some scrap and useful items, other times your crew will die and you are left missing a person. This type of thing overshadows the entire game, making you feel cheated at times.
But with all those things put together with an amazing soundtrack this game is a wonderful thing to pick up for something to do, and you will not be dissapointed. Unless you hate roguelikes or risk/reward situations, in that case avoid this game like the plague, as most of the game is Risk/Reward. Well worth the money, and even more so when it goes on sale.

Just when I though "Tales of the Borderlands" was the epitome of greatness of the Telltale games, along comes "Game Of Thrones!"
Pros:
- Amazing story that presents the hardest decision making of any Telltale game to date!
- Telling the story from multiple character points of view actually works!  Didn't work in "Tales of the Borderlands," but glad it worked here!!!
Cons:
- Throws you in the deep end and you have no idea who any of the characters are, or what's going on.  When I started the game, I thought I may have made a mistake playing it before I'd even watched one episode of the "Game Of Thrones" TV series.  I'm so glad I stuck through the initial confusion, because I was treated to the best Telltale game ever!  Once you get past the first character's introduction story, and you transition to the second character, everything becomes clear.  Stick it out!
- Not having enough time to make decisions in dialogue choices.  I loved the way the "Mass Effect" games gave you all the time in the world to pick your choice of what to say.  "Game of Thrones" gives you a limited time, and way less than even some of their other games such as, "The Walking Dead," and "The Wolf Among Us."  "Tales of the Borderlands" was just as bad.  I wish Telltale could add a difficulty option in the main menu that would give you the choice of picking limited or unlimited time to make dialogue choices.  I think this would make their games perfect.
If you play any Telltale game, make it this one!  Replaces "Tales of the Borderlands" as their best game ever!!!  Still, play "Tales of the Borderlands also.  Heck, you may as well add "The Walking Dead" seasons and "The Wolf Among Us," too.  All quality!!!

Alan Wake's American Nightmare takes place after the original game. You are in Arizona and need to defeat Mr. Grinch, who is in fact your double. He uses your identity to be you in the real life. He has both your life, and your wife. You need to find a way to stop him.
If you have not played the original game, I recommend you to at least read the wiki to understand the story. It is very weird, and you will be more implied in the story if you already know the characters and why you are in this world.
The combat mechanism is exactly the same than in Alan Wake. I played the original game on the Xbox 360. I used my controller to play this game on PC, and the controls did not change a bit. You will be familiar in few seconds with them.
The atmosphere is quite the same than in Alan Wake. However, there is a lot more ammo. There are ammo caches everywhere and they regenerate by themselves. You will never need to run away for your life. The difficulty is also a problem. If you are used to these types of games, play it on hard. The medium difficulty gives no challenge. I think that I died only once throughout the game. It takes few hours to complete it, that said you will play the game 3 times! I will not tell more about this, but that is the main downside of this game. I would have like more to play a shorter game than a fake long one.
The graphics and sound is good. It has not change from the previous game though.
There is a challenge mode in which you have to survive the longer you can. That does not really interest me, so I will not speak of it here. I do not find it valuable.
Because that the game has been lengthen artificially, I cannot really recommend it. The survival feeling that you got in Alan Wake has been lost with the many ammo caches that can be found throughout the game. If you really want to know what happens after the original game, I would recommend you to read the wiki on it, that would save you precious time.

It might be that this is the game's vision but this pretentious ideology only saves the creators the time of actually creating more good ideas and locations that would make the story actually interesting.  I lament this fact because the game has really good functionality that is better in the first game, but throws it all away by literally reusing the same locations over and over and over again. The American nightmare picks up a couple of years after the events of the first game. Alan is still trapped in limbo - in the dark place, but evidently some parts of his mind attempt to escape the hold of the darkness. When he was first touched by darkness he spawned Mr. Scratch - an evil but charismatic,enigmatic as well as a "better" version of himself as Mr. Scratch himself put it.
Mr. Scratch is trying to get out into the world and replace Wake who is thought dead by everyone except Barry. Wake finds himself in Arizona where weird phenomena keeps happening. He finds himself in a horror episode created by Mr. Scratch. ok, no more spoilers but there are a couple of twists in the story, and then there are more...twists..again and again....
There are only three more characters in the game so it feels pretty desolate. Pretty soon the game turns into an arcade shoot. The ammo is plentiful (there are actually ammo and supply respawns throughout the game), the open-worldliness of the first map kinda takes away the feeling of accomplishment. You keep looking for the pages of the manuscript that Wake keeps writing in the dark place and use it to unlock better weapons as well as knowledge about what to do next.
There are about 5 new enemies. There are spiders, there are those who can split into multiple versions of themselves, those who can stand 9 feet tall and wild large chain saws, those who turn into birds and those who can throw stink bombs, I guess.
What's interesting is how you are able to pick up on the events of the world through radio shows and disturbing camcorder videos done by Mr. Scratch which were an absolute blast to watch and there are plenty of them. They used plenty of live video here which is unheard of in 99% of games. I also particularly enjoyed the determinism vs. free will arguments between Wake and the astronomer as well as on the radio. Wake basically argued that the absence of free will is irrelevant given the fact that the character knows nothing about the next set of set deterministic events.
In any case the atmosphere is there, but it also feels kind of cheap, the desert is just too boring. I also found myself disinterested for the first couple of hours but then I kept playing and kept getting sucked in. It took me about 5.5 hours to finish the game. The game also does a pretty good job of explaining why the first game looked [played] like a TV show or a drama/thriller movie. Wake explains that he is able to fight the Taken effectively (and dodge attacks) because that was a small semi-realistic kernel of the main protagonist that helps propel the story forward. So many more things can make sense now for those who didn't really get the original game.
There is also a survival mode. You are given 10 minutes to fight off the taken at various locations until the sunrise. It can be fun but I doubt you will be playing it more than a few times. I put the game into the hard category because there are a few frustrating spots in the game (especially the last 20 minutes) but you do feel pretty good when you survive multiple attacks with the last few bullets.
All in all. I would recommend this to anyone who enjoyed the first game.

Star Raiders was one of my favorite games on the old Atari 8-bit systems. Packed into a measly 8K of ROM was a surprisingly detailed and complex space dogfighting game. When I saw that Atari was releasing an updated version for the PC, I was both excited and wary. All too often companies dig up a popular title from their vaults and try to squeeze more money out of it (anyone remember Knight Rider 2000?)
Alas, that's exactly what Atari has done with Star Raiders. This version of the game is about as unlike the original as you could possibly get while still flying a space fighter. Now it has a story, it's mission-based, the fighter can transform into different modes and there are cutscenes. There are also a number of new types of enemies to fight, including capital ships. I never got to a point where I could go into hyperspace or use the Galactic Chart or Long Range Scanner, if those things even exist in the game. While the original Star Raiders managed to squeeze the entire game into a mere 8,192 BYTES, this new version weighs in at nearly a full gigabyte.
Graphics are OK, if rather uninspired. It seemed a bit hard to figure out what I was looking at sometimes, with dark ships against the dark background of space, but fortunately enemies have boxes around them so you can always figure out where you need to shoot. The game really looks like a direct port from the X-Box.
The biggest flaw with Star Raiders is the horrendous controls. I could not get the game to recognize the rudder, throttle or hat controls on my Microsoft Sidewinder Precision Pro joystick. It also wouldn't recognize the additional buttons on my Logitech G700 gaming mouse or my Logitech Dual Action gamepad. Without the rudder or throttle, attempting to fly with the joystick is impossible, while trying to fly with the mouse felt like I was piloting a Mack truck through molasses. Keyboard? Don't make me laugh.
As far as gameplay, I really wouldn't know. I couldn't make it past the third tutorial because the controls were so utterly abysmal I couldn't track the enemy fighters to shoot them down. It might have been an interesting game if the controls actually worked.
This game has been out for two years and the publisher has never released an update.  Don't waste your money on it.
I enjoyed my time with it, not sure if it's worth full price because it's pretty short, but check it out on sale for few bucks!

Let me start off by saying that this is more of a party game then a full fledged fighter or anything.  That's the beauty of Lethal League though is it aims to keep the fun simple with a delightful mechanic and well animated and imaginative characters and music.  Here are my lists of Pros and Cons by Catagory
Gameplay- Pros:  This game is fast paced and has a mechanic revolving around a ball that kills upon impact from another player's succesful swing and hit.  the object of the game is to knock out the other fighters ala super smash bros or other arcade fighters by smashing the ball their way in hopes that they will not have the reaction time to swing back and be slammed out of the arena.  The gameplay is fast and addictive and best experienced with friends and is highly based on reaction time and the ability to angle the ball or juke other players with the "bunt" function or special hits that build up as you hit/bunt the ball.  In short it's a fun arcadey baseball deathmatch game with a simple but unique mechanic.
Gameplay-  Cons:  The single player "challenge" mode(this games version of super smash bros's classic mode) leaves much to be desired and is quite simple, and while the ai can be challennging for a new player at first it is never as difficult as a real player leaving multiplayer the best option.  There are multiple game modes but most players seldom use or even have fun with them, and the game could use more content on the single player and gameplay mode selection side overall.
Graphics- Pros:  The art style and characters are lovingly inspired from a variety of sources most notably I see hints of super smash bros characters and jetset radio style stlye.  You have a baseball loving tough kid, a woman that uses a boombox on a stick as a bat, a man with a piece of candy for a head, and a cyborg alligator, and a robot(who uses a skateboard as his bat and means to get around), and a man named Dice...who oddly enough uses a ping pong paddle.  The art is lovingly design and the stages and characters have a lot of personality
Graphics- Cons:  The characters could use a few more animation touch ups and overall new animations I'd argue and the art style is sometimes used to cover up what is a seemingly simple engine, the stages could use some work too and I feel some of them while inspired could use even more touchups and design changes both aesthetically, and gameplay wise(they are all essentially boxes)
Music/Audio- Pros:  This is where the game really shines in the music department.  If you enjoyed Jetset Radio at all you will feel more then welcome and at home here then you have in a game since that series.  The music is incredibly well done and produced and I'll sometimes find myself wanting to play certain stages in the game just to hear the tunes.  "Ordinary Days" is a personal favorite of mine though all the tracks of each stage and menu are seething with excellent production and unique "garage future" tones.
Music Audio- Cons:  The characters are lacking in some voice overs and you'll often hear the same voice clips over and over again.  This is not all bad as some lines are quite clever but I really wish the dev team would give them a bit more life with some new and alternate lines.
----
Overall the game is pretty fun if you have some buddies itching for some crazy arcadey multiplayer.  It can get pretty intense as the ball speed ramps up higher and higher until the stages are tearing at the seams.  I don't recommend purchasing it at full price however, I would wait for a price drop or a sale to pick this rad, lovable, indie arcade fighter in the future.

C'mon mean marine!  Get back into the action as you try to find your way back after being separated from the rest of your group.
This game has a lot of guns to play with.  Autocannon for those sweet bursts of explosive ammo that can kill in one shot. Arclites that will not only roast up your enemy but the lingering flame effects on the ground will continue to hurt any enemies walking through.  Each gun does something a bit differently and you must decide which one works bests for your style and situation.
Graphics look pretty sweet especially on a nice video card.  Lots of explosions and flying guts for your viewing pleasure.
RPG flavor where you can level up your soldier in a multitude of ways to help augment your playstyle.  There doesn't seem to be any "bad" choices here as it is all up to how you want to play the game.
Play again as a different type of soldier.  You can pick the all around Assault class, Demolition class or even be the Terminator class (once unlocked).  Each class sure to help mix up your game and also give you new ways to make those alien heads explode.
The greatest downfall of this game is that there is no online multiplayer.  You can still local co-op this game however.
Overall this is still a fun game to play and at 20 bucks not breaking the bank either.  Developers have always listened to their fans and will sure to make even better games in the future.

Very good game indeed.  It is most unussual in that in most games you start off with a nice easy tutorial and the game gradually gets harder.  In lost castle it's the opposite.  You start off with nothing and you will find the first half hour very difficult but then with each death you get mana points to upgrade.  So after an hour of playing it then becomes very enjoyable slaying all the beasts that you previously had so much trouble against at the start of the game.  I found this very rewarding to see this progress being made as each playthrough got easier and easier.  In the 4 hours I have sunk in I have so far got to the 3rd world out of 4. Yes you heard me right a fish!!  I was like a little kid at xmas as my face lit up.  I grasped the 2 foot beauty with both hands and charged into the dungeon to unleash hell. GOOD GAME BUT NOT WHAT I EXPECTED
Basically its a twin stick shooter style shoot em up but with a "chore" system, i came in expecting a fun shoot em up with standard upgrades and skill point and horde of enemy, what i got is a mix of good and cumbersome game.
WHAT I LIKE:
- killing enemy is satisfying, the gun sound, the effect, the feel, overall its great.
- upgrade is plenty, you have 3 tab and each tab give you a lot of active and passive skill to play around with.
- environment is amazing, some stage is pretty big and open so you can roam around look for stuff etc.
- 4 classes each with different playstyle.
WHAT I DONT LIKE:
- you can only have 2 weapon (why?)
- drone system is a chore, like it or not you will use it because the game pretty much forced you to do so.
- infinite enemy spawn, probably the biggest let down for me.
- threat meter, on paper it sounds amazing but the meter fill up too fast (thus the drone system) and can be game breaking for some people, in one instance i got full meter and the game send me 3 THREE boss enemy from previous stage, it took me everything just to kill one because the boss has insane armor unless you attack from behind but, the boss is pretty agile and will melee you with 100% accuracy if you get too close (unless you sprint), on top of that every 7-10 seconds it let out a roar which spawn either 5+ normal enemy or 2-3 tanky enemy. And the game just literally give me THREE, i have no choice but to run away and speedrun the whole stage which defeat the purpose of shoot em up game.
3/5

You may ask "What makes this game different from any other bullet-hell game?" and my answer is simply: The controls.
While that may not seem like much at first, the controls in this game are different for every character, which there is a diverse array of. From flicking the controller stick to fire your revolver and tapping to reload each bullet, to spinning the stick (huehuehue yes I know just grow up wont you?!) to fire your minigun, and having the precision accuracy of the sniper using your mouse. The game also features a great Arcade mode with leaderboards and round to round progression in the form of upgradable stats (Such as incindenary rounds, bullet velocity, and even starting on horseback.), a versus mode for sweet pvp action, and a story mode to embark upon! Greyfox Review... the first one I do in English
I've experienced some Maker-games so far and can say that I mostly look at an interesting setting or storyline before I mention to buy it or to play it. For most games in this genre there is a special way how I evaluate Maker-games, but instead of showing you this list (I didn't ever wrote it down anyway) I will take this game as example...
The little driving part in the first minutes of gameplay was well designed, also was the town Greyfox. You can interact with almost every item in this game and get one or two lines with a good description about it. And then there was some hilarious moments and little details I enjoyed. But unfortunately - the game is short. One single hour in fact. But because it has three different endings it is worth to re-play it... atleast one time I think.
Besides the driving part (with way too stupid AI and bad mechanics), gameplay is more offside the road. You get some little side-quests here and there, rewarded with an achievement and that's it. No mini games or puzzles... unfortunately.
But where it really leaks, is the story. The fact that you can play as different charakters and judge over their misdeeds whether they should kill themselfes or not is quite enjoyable... but was it really necessary? Killing or leaving those people doesn't feel right. What if you were able to save everyone and fix their lives again (active)... Speak to your family, show them that you aren't just an eldery♥♥♥♥♥♥in a retirement home... Have a last day together with your poisoned husband to bring love to 'em - a last time again. Maybe it is kitchy but better than just leave them and forget them again. I mean you won't ever get any clues how you were able to do this or why you were chosen to do so. It doesn't feel alive or reasoned. So why not? At the end it's better than nothing.
Price: Okay -> You got your money spent on two or three hours; one filled with the actual story, the last one is probably filled with skipping text massages to gain the rest of the achievements... maybe wait for a sale.
Rating: Average -> What is there more to say? We have a interesting setting but no answers to the story... you want more in the end and unfortunately there was so much potentioal wasted... that's why for me it's just an ordinary game. Go for the achievements if you want, or else, just leave it.

This may surprise some readers, but I feel that Company of Heroes 2 was a diamond in the rough. It had a myriad of issues- offending Russians, poor optimization on launch, a surprising amount of DLC, and Relic’s usual inability to balance their game. COH2 was also- at least on the surface- quite similar to the original game.
At the same time, Company of Heroes 2 is an amazing and unique experience. There is no other game with the same depth of micro, no other game with such immersive graphics and sound, and no other game where the singleplayer and the multiplayer are equally fantastic and fleshed out. So many people cry out about the decline of the RTS without realizing that the genre has been reborn. I have my gripes with the game, but Relic’s vision is something that more developers need to have.

I REALLY wish there was some sort of neutral review option instead of the up or down thumbs. Let me just say that this game is extremely fun. It is extremely polished and it will keep you coming back for more time and time again when you die. And yes, you will die....ALOT. The main problem i have with this game is how it always seems like your opponents dont play by the same rules as you. This is laughably apparent when you encounter the flagship, but more on that later.
This is a game where the RNG (random number generator or random number god) holds your fate in its hand almost every time you do a jump. It does not matter how decked out your ship is, how many max level crew you have or how prepared you THINK you are. Like i said in the previous paragraph, the game does not play by the same rules as you, and you will find many enounters that feel unfair, or some that are flat out impossible to win against depending on what ship you pick.
And that leads me to the games boss, the flagship. If you manage to get to this behemoth of a ship, you will probably do what i did the first time i encountered it. First you will be awe struck at how big and how many systems and weapons it has, and then when it fires that first volley of lasers and missles which seem to never end, you will sit back, laugh out loud and roll your eyes. I am by no means saying the flagship cant be beaten, because it most definitely can. The problem is in order to beat it there are really only a small list of ship "builds" that are effective, and even with those setups, grasping victory can seem very difficult. Alot of the time you have to rely on luck, because while you think that 55% evasion you have actually equals 55%, it will feel like 10% when a full volley of missles and 2 volleys of lasers all impact with almost no misses whatsoever.
As i said, the game is very fun, its definitely worth your time, and you will come back for more no matter how stupidly frustrating it can be.  Just realize that all the planning and ship upgrades in the world are just one or two jumps from ending up as space debris at any given moment.

Epic Showdown is a 3rd person shooter/action game, developed by Naloki and uses the Unreal engine. The game offers you as the player the option to play one of 4 separate characters, in a number of different settings and locales, along with a couple of different game modes.
The combat in Epic Showdown is your typical 3rd person shooter: you point at what you want dead, you click the left mouse button, and then they tend to drop. Nothing too special! Instead of enemies dropping weapons however, each character comes equipped with 4 of them, all of which do something different, but they all fit the characters they are attached to. After all, you wouldn’t see the mage of the game holding out a pair of pistols, as that would just completely defeat the point of him being a spell-caster.
Now, it’s a little difficult to ignore the character design in this game, and you’ll know why now, as here’s the list:
•	Rotheart – An evil necromancer with a pumpkin on his head, with access to magical abilities.
•	Mrs Groundfire – An elderly lady equipped with a minigun. Yes! A minigun!!
•	Boris Porkov – A medieval pig warrior, whom has access to an assortment of melee weapons.
•	Sonny “Ricochet” Banani – A monkey who just so happens to be a mobster as well, equipped with a couple of pistols, a shotgun, an SMG, as well as a Molotov to tickle that inner-arsonist
Each character is equipped with their own 4 different weapons, all of which are specified for one character and one character alone. This makes for a different experience with each and every character, meaning that you will get some variety when you pick a different individual to play for yourself.
There isn’t too much variety when it comes to game modes, one of which being survival, which is a category that has wave defence and objective inside it. The gist of that being, you either play until you die, or you do the objective the game sets for you. Crypt mode is a little different, as your main task isn’t just kill things and keep yourself alive. Instead, you’re effectively thrown into a maze, which you have to somehow make your way to the end of, while many nasty creatures come to ruin your run.
In survival mode you can pick and choose one of 5 pre-built stages for you to play in, whereas in crypt mode it’s procedurally generated. I know it says it’s randomly generated on the store page, but it’s not. The game takes tile-sets from a predetermined pool to make your crypt level, as I’ve seen the same area multiple times on different runs without any change, meaning that the areas in the dungeon aren’t random if they’ve already been designed. That being said, it’s nice to have a bit of change here and there when it comes to the stages, so it’s nice to have some procedurally generated dungeons to keep the life of the game going a little more.
Graphically, the game definitely isn’t anything special, and can probably go as far as ugly. The animations are a bit stiff, and just doesn’t look all that great, regardless of if it’s a walking or running animation, or an attack, they just all look rather clunky and aren’t all that special to witness. Character design is interesting, but the characters themselves, along with whatever enemies you come in contact with don’t look particularly great and that won’t be changing, no matter how many different creatures you come across.
The 5 stages for the most part are all different from one another, so it’s nice to see the different stages, since one is focused around ice, and another one revolves around fire, so thankfully not every stage looks the same or has the same colour pallet for you to deal with. Where the stages don’t shine so much is in their design, as I’ve found myself clipping into objects numerous times, and even at one point was almost completely stuck in a corner, with little to no way out until spamming the jump button for around 2 minutes solved the problem. Even if you can solve that problem while playing, they shouldn’t be there in the first place. When you’re being stuck on something that you really shouldn’t get stuck on can quickly get frustrating, especially when you’re being followed by a train of mobs that want your guts for garters.
Speaking of mobs, the AI in this game is incredibly simplistic. They do little to nothing more than just walking up to you, a lot of the time in single file, just to bash you on the head. Their AI isn’t complex at all, meaning that you can pretty much just back away from any enemy coming towards you, and kill them without any trouble. Up until the point you get clipped on something that you shouldn’t, which you’ll find will quickly frustrate you when that’s the reason you’ve just died.
One serious problem the game has is bugs. They’re everywhere, and it really needs to be cleaned up a fair bit to make the game more enjoyable. For instance, when selecting a character in Survival mode, the character model doesn’t change until the moment you hit select and get in-game, so for a first time player, you have little to no idea who you’re picking. Then, once you’ve picked your character, the character model that floats in this tube that you’ll see when picking a character stays on the level, even after you’ve started.
These bugs don’t really affect gameplay, but this next one does. With Ricochet you have access to an SMG, which obviously will have ammo tied to it. If you use every single bullet in your SMG, but don’t let go of left mouse click, you’ll switch out to your pistol, but it will fire like your SMG until you let go. Oh, and once you have let go, all the sounds that you can hear from then on is multiple layers of the same shooting sound effect being looped over and over again, at a surprisingly high volume. You may be able to cheat, but your ears will be paying the price if you’re not careful.
Along with bugs, you’ll come across a few grammar and punctual mistakes throughout. Not to the degree where you can’t understand a single word on the screen, but enough so to at least mention it, in the hopes that it might get sorted in time.
Overall, Epic Showdown shows some promise down the line, but it really does need to have those bugs sorted out, sooner rather than later. However, if you don't take the game seriously at all, and just enjoy it for the lighthearted theme of it all, then you'll probably enjoy it a little more. I am going to recommend the game, but that's down to the fact that I'm putting hope that the game will be improved down the line. Plus, I enjoy supporting indie developers. If you're still on the fence, be sure to check out some gameplay. You'll know from there whether you want to try the game out for yourself.

Another very good game in this series.
Let's do the good first.
If you played Re;Birth1 you already know how to play this and can easily jump right in. Jump I have not found a use for yet aside from just wanting to make your character bounce in the air... or panty shots, if you're into that. Combat is fairly fluid and easy to learn, and you get new skills at a fairly regular pace. There are 3 different types of attacks, Rush, Power, and Break. Rush fills the EXE gauge, Power does more health damage, and Break does more guard damage. That along with 4 elemental properties, statuses, and being either physical or magic makes for a rather interesting mix for combat. You also have a reserve character slot for each character in your party, which you can swap out to if the party member is alive.
Graphics are nice, not the best but definitely good for an anime style game. Some of the areas and characters look amazing, and some EXE attacks are just beautiful to watch. Music and sound effects are good, nothing you will remember, but fitting for the atmosphere of the areas or what you are doing. Voice acting is pretty decent, with most of the characters having well written, if sometimes cheesy as all hell, dialogue. There is also plenty of tongue in cheek humor and breaking of the 4th wall simply for the fun of it. Various enemies are reused over and over, with only palette swaps to really mark the difference in how they look, but that is standard for many RPGs.
There are a ton of playable characters. I have 13 right now and I am fairly certain there's at least another 7. Party size is 4 characters, with another 4 in reserve. Thankfully ALL characters that are alive get XP, regardless of if they're in the party or not.
Stella's Dungeon is a very nice little addition to this game, even if you do not control Stella directly it is entertaining to do. Equip her gear, send her on her way, and do whatever until she is beaten or comes back with loot.
Now the bad...
This game is almost a direct clone of Re;Birth1, if you did not like 1, you are not going to like this. Combat, a list of characters, and various other things are all the same, and if you played the first one you are going to be going "haven't I done this before" every now and then.
I mentioned the large amount of characters earlier, if you plan to keep them all up to date on gear you are going to be spending an obscene amount of currency. Another slight issue is with so many characters many will level up at the same time, and wanting to keep their combo abilities and finishers up to date can be annoying when 5+ characters all get new abilities after a single fight.
It is incredibly easy to overlevel your characters. And I mean insanely easy. I have not farmed for money or XP, just items now and then to finish off quests (quests give currency and items, not XP). I just got a new character and my characters are a good 12-15 levels above her. It should be noted you can use the plan system to weaken of strengthen the enemies.
That being said the story is different, there are new characters, new enemies, and I would buy it again.

"101 hours in and he's not recommending it? What's this guy smoking?"
I know, I know. But despite all the memes, I really don't think this game is worth thirty bucks - much less the extra fifteen they try to squeeze out of you via DLC.
Story:
The story is as bland, light-hearted, and generic as they come. It's your standard, run-of-the-mill "save the world" plot, but its unique writing is a large factor in this series's popularity. Unfortunately, it's also a double-edged sword. As you probably know already, this game breaks the fourth wall fairly often, with characters constantly coming up with excuses to make reference to the fact that they're in a game. This, however, gets old. Fast. Especially when you realize that half these references were never in the original Japanese to begin with.
It also makes fun of several tropes often found in anime, but forgets that it's also shamelessly playing them straight. For example, Noire is occasionally ridiculed in-game as being a tsundere (or at least, what that word's definition has morphed into), but that doesn't change the fact that she is one. Same thing for Older Brother and Younger Brother - their existence serves to make fun of male characters who obsess over boobs, but they themselves are male characters that obsess over boobs (something we don't need, since we have the player for that). News flash: pointing out your own stupidity doesn't change the fact that you're stupid.
Where the writing isn't annoying, it's lazy. Who are these six people and why do they know Neptune? Oh, they're from another dimension, so no biggie. This will never again be questioned or even mentioned. Uh-oh, we're in a pickle! It's okay, we just need a Shares ex machina. (The game itself makes fun of this, but still - it happens.)
But Kazoo, you argue, all that is just the game being silly and light-hearted! Can't you just have some fun for once in your life? Well, let me ask you this: would you eat candy - the same candy - for every meal for an entire week? You'd get sick of it, right? The problem with this game's story is that it's too one-note; it refuses to take itself seriously. There aren't really any dramatic tonal shifts, so the stakes never seem to be very high. It's hard to take interest in a story that's the same all the way through.
Assets:
Many JRPGs reuse enemy sprites at some point because they just didn't have the time, money, or creativity to come up with more. Oftentimes, that's understandable - when it's a rare occurrence, at least. In Neptunia, recycling of sprites is the norm. There are dozens of Dogoo enemies with only three different sprites between them. You'll fight the same orange flower in dungeon after dungeon, with maybe a new coat of paint to tell the difference. Giant dragons? Well, every last one of them looks exactly the same - they aren't even recolored. Even the (non-main-character) bosses are reused! I posit that once you finish Chapter 2, you'll have seen almost every significant enemy sprite the game has to offer.
And it's not just enemy sprites. It's dungeons, too. Now, reusing dungeon textures isn't as bad a problem as reusing enemy sprites, but reusing dungeon LAYOUTS is even worse. Every last cave dungeon in the game is exactly the same, with only a few minor differences. Every last forest dungeon in the game is exactly the same, with only a few minor differences - and so on and so forth. Out of the 36 dungeons in the game, there are only (off the top of my head) nine different ones. Coupled with the recycled enemy sprites, this is GRUELING. It eliminates the fun of exploring a new dungeon. How can I get excited about it when I already know what it will be before I even enter?
Gameplay:
But this is a JRPG. The most important part about it is the gameplay. And to the game's credit, it has solid battle mechanics that seem mundane at first, but quickly become complex and interesting once you get slaughtered in the Colosseum for the first time. It's easy to understand, but it has aspects to it that make the more hardcore JRPG players salivate. You don't have to be good at JRPGs to have fun playing this game.
Unfortunately, you collide - hard - into a brick wall near the endgame. Maybe I just suck at it, but I am convinced that certain parts of the game's later content (lookin' at you, Zeca Ruins 2) are designed to be impossible (or at least prohibitively hard) unless you buy the DLC. Which I didn't do, 'cause paid DLC is an evil concept that never deserved to exist in the first place. So if I'm getting slaughtered effortlessly by trash mobs at level 99, why should I feel the need to get Nepgear to level 99 too? Why should I feel the need to NG+ again and get Rom and Ram? Granted, I'm only talking about non-story dungeons here, but still.
Perhaps it'd be easier on me if I bought better weapons for my characters. But with said weapons ranging from one to five million credits each, I'd have a lot of grinding in my future. A ridiculous amount, really, even by JRPG standards. And since this is an enormous price increase from the next tier down, the message is abundantly clear: either you fork over more cash, or you waste days on end trying to save up for a better weapon that will only MARGINALLY increase your chances of surviving an ordinary battle.
After 101 hours of Neptunia, I'm looking back and wishing I could have them back. I really wanted to like this game - the range of character customization options is insane, the character designs are cute and full of life, the battle system is fun - but the story and the world are unbelievably boring. The cherry on top? The translator is incompetent at best and infuriating at worst. Don't buy this game. Not for thirty bucks. If it goes on sale, maybe - but personally, I'd recommend you take your business elsewhere altogether.

Ah Grim Dawn.  As of this writing, I have about 25 hours in this game.  I've gotten through the first chapter, having defeated the first really major, plot point boss, the equivalent of the Butcher, for those of you familiar with Diablo 3, though I may be overselling the importance of that particular boss.  Nevertheless, having co-oped my way into the second area, I have to say that I struggle to go any further.  I want to like this game, I really do.  I love the very customizable class system, I love the art work and design aesthetic, I enjoyed the story, and the gameplay, as a Diablo clone, is solid.  But I struggle with this game, and for all the things that they do right here, the biggest problem is the pacing.  The game drags on, giving little tidbits of plot here and there in the midst of long stretches of grind.  Getting to and through that first major boss was such a draining experience that my partner has not returned for more, and I find that I struggle to work my way through solo.  I want to like this game, I want to play this game, but the reward for the grind is just not quite worth the effort.  I will continue to beat my head against this game, because I really do like it, but I sometimes just find the idea of jumping in exhausting.
TLDR:  Too much grind to reveal not enough story makes this a slough where it should be an enjoyable slaughter-filled romp.
I recommend this game only if you love the hack and slash gameplay enough to grind out the story.  Otherwise, don't bother.

When a sequel is released, there are a couple of different options you can take.  It can be a sequel in name only, be loosely connected on the first title, or be a direct sequel, and a few other options.  Hyperdimension Neptunia is a little bit of one and two, in that you have to play the first to understand anything as the game sure doesn't take the time to introduce you to everyone again('If you're playing this, you've played the first' is the logic) and pretty much everything's changed, as the game takes place in another dimension, so every event that you remember in the first game goes out the window.  Some facts are still the same though, such as characters and personalities.  Since this game is trying to be a sequel, it's only fair that we look at it as a sequel, with comparisons to the first game.  The 'feel' of the game is the same, so graphics, sounds, those are pretty much the exact same, this will be more focused on the differences in gameplay and story.
So the story feels a little shorter in this one, but there's more to it as well.  Characters are introduced earlier and have much more time to get their personality fleshed out..  Although one-dimensional characters are always one-dimensional.  The well-written nature has only been improved.  In fact, there are optional characters that you can scoop up along the story that have no story presence, but plenty of optional scenes that showcase their own personality.  It's a good solution from the previous game in where you suddenly got 6 characters who have a total of 9 lines.  This way you have all your characters show their personality and quirks.  However, characters unlocked through special means that also aren't related to the story still get shunned.  It was a bit of a shocker when my party almost doubled in size in the span of a few hours of gameplay.
The plot could be described as "Team Rocket is trying to destroy the world, and Jesse&James try to ruin your day, every day."  The Jesse&James in this game are fought about 10 times as you two have to be at the same area, so you always run into each other.  Pretty much every part of the story involves them somehow.  They're pretty bothersome, but needed to move the story along.
Later in the game, depending on certain objectives that you complete(Possible to achieve without realizing it, but unlikely) you can branch out the story conclusions, and one of them is just heart-wrenching.  The feels felt like I was watching Clannad, but everyone dies instead of just having sad stories with happy endings.  Just sadness and feels in this ending.  The basic plot isn't better or worse, just different.
Gameplay hasn't changed much.  Battle system is the same, but has the addition of a fourth character, so fights are even easier.  As long as you kill every monster you see, you’ll have a hard time losing a fight.  The 'use Ram to get perks' is still there, with one important perk added: Exp and gold gotten when you use the ‘destroy enemy’ perk.  Otherwise, the enemy dies and you get nothing.  Conversely, the jumping star perk(2x jump height) is used for nothing at all, except to look at Uni’s underwear for a tenth of a second longer;  Feels like they improved it while leaving the old stuff there. Also, unlocking tougher dungeons follows more of a path this time, as opposed to extra bosses being all over the place and level 100 monsters in basic upgraded areas;  General improvements all-around in that area, although relying on hidden items to give plans to upgrade dungeons dungeons is a terrible idea, as the low chance of it appearing means that you HAVE to read a walkthrough to continue to upgrade dungeons.  Next to no chance of bumbling into it.
... Of course, there are still 10,000 hats for you to get, but the amount of unique/reference costumes seems to have gone down in favor of recolors.
One of the new things introduced was Stella's Dungeon.  This little game is best described as an idle game.  You give Stella some equipment and send her off to a dungeon.  After some real-time has passed, she comes back and if she beat the dungeon, she gives you cool loot and keeps everything.  If she fails, you keep the stuff you found but lose all your current equipment.  Pretty cute idea on a little bit of extra farming and some bonus equipment, but the problem is actually that it takes too long.  I downloaded the DLC which made the dungeons take half the time needed and Stella doesn't lose equipment upon failure.  Even with this, it still took almost a week and a half to do all of her dungeons.  Without the DLC, it'll take about a month.  Sure, it's an idle game designed as a little coffee break, but it should at least be timed so that by the time you're super powerful and done everything, it still doesn't take two weeks just to finish it.  Good idea, ultimately pointless.  If you want the achievement, just get the DLC.

More effort was put into dialogue this time around, which is pretty nice, but still isn’t perfect.  Strangely, in the box Compa refers to Nepgear as Ge-Ge(Like calling Neptune Nep-Nep), but she says Gear-Chan.  I guess that's okay.
For me, these are pretty much the big or most notable changes going from Rebirth1 to Rebirth2.  Everything else is pretty much the same, and I'm fine with that, as it should be pretty much the same with more improvements.  So would I recommend this game?  I do!  I'm sure that there will be more improvements to come, and if you didn't like it and you saw the reason in the above, well it's fixed so you should go play this then. Alan Wake's American Nightmare is quite a far cry from the original. The last one focused on story telling and atmoshpere whereas the main focus of this one is combat. In the last game, combat was simple. Shine your light on the guy long enough, and then shoot him. In this one, all sorts of new taken arise and are ready for the fight. One of them actually get's stronger when he comes into contact with your light. He splits into two weaker versions of himself, which both lack a shield. Another is a behemoth with a rather large saw. Another will lob darkness grenades at you. Each will require good timing and skill to take down.
In this lighter offering, the story suffers and the longevity is reduced. The environments are recycled as well due to the plot. Each time you think you can escape the town, time resets and you have to do everything all over again, except with all your old weapons.
Overall, it's repetitive and the story suffers, but there's far more gameplay here for those of you who felt the last one was just an interactive movie. Heck, there's even a nighttime survival gamemode which isn't half bad. Overall, I'd give it a 7/10.

A Fistful of Gun - The Righteous Review
A few months ago I found a stream on twitch by this guy, Paul Hart, whom I had never heard about before. He was designing some graphics that seem to be based around the wonderful Sergio Leone spaghetti westerns of the 1960s, The Good The Bad and The Ugly, A fistful of Dollars, Once Upon a Time in America and others. In the background he was also streaming some music from those same films by the incredible Ennio Morricone. The art was good. The art was very good. I then realised this was not just some static images, this was all for a game that he was also developing. I have to admit, I was instantly hooked. My favourite movie genre was being recreated in my favourite pastime, video gaming.
Fast forward a few months to present time and I get to present to you the A Fistful of Gun review and if asked to sum up my feelings in one word, that word would be, wow.
A Fistful of Gun – For a Few Gun More, is in simple terms a top down shooter where you and up to nine, yes nine, other players get to wield the baddest, most righteous gunslingers in the wicked wild west. Simple terms however do this game no justice, A Fistful of Gun is one of the most frenetic, hilarious, addictive and complete video games I have ever had the pleasure to play.
To say that Fistful of Gun is a multiplayer game would be doing it a severe injustice though at it’s heart it really is meant to be played with others, both locally through a wonderful system of couch co-op or online with fully optimised net code. Have no fears that this is yet another Indie game with tacked on online play as it is not, Fistful of Gun plays incredibly well online and offers a wealth of modes and fun, however I shall start with the story mode.
Taking the role of one of eleven characters you play the part of a lone gunman with one task, to stop the evil railroad Baron, Clayton Boon, and avenge the ‘righteous psychosis’ of those he has wronged. To do this you must traverse thirteen miles of barren western deserts, hokey townships, corrupt lawmen, arrow toting red Indians and much much more. Along the way you will find pickups to upgrade your guns, barrels of Whiskey that really test your drunken gun-slinging skills, and even a very powerful drug induced high that will have you trippin’ all the way to your characters tombstone. After it’s initial release we are also promised access to Spirit Animals to help you on your quest. All of this is done through a top down, almost bullet hell game play filled with colour, and extremely pretty pixel styled graphics that invoke a retro gaming feel but a very modern and fast gaming experience.
Levels in A Fistful of Gun vary extensively in looks and feel and you will find that what worked on the previous one will not do so on the next. This makes the game feel fresh every time you progress and each play-through is always a little different which can and will keep you coming back for more. Top this off with an excellent high score list that keeps track of all global players and your friends and you have more than one reason to keep coming back for more.
In addition to the single player Story section of the game we also have Local and Online Arcade mode which involves multiple levels of gunslinger action across all the varied themed areas and with harder A.I. as you progress. The arcade mode can also be played solo or with up to nine other players through online play or Fistfuls unique control style where all nine players can couch around just the one PC and use a combination of purely mouse control, pure keyboard control and of course full game controller support. I won’t lie, the controls can get confusing and each character has varying ways of being played so for some a controller is the only way, for others mouse and keyboard is your only option. This forces players to prefer one character over another but with eleven to choose from there is always a character for everyone’s style and abilities.
The other main online mode is Versus and as the name suggests it is you versus everyone else but as this is A Fistful of Gun the areas are also spiced up with TNT, Trains, Mexican outlaws and much more, all designed to make your job of killing your opponents as hard as possible and as much fun as it can be, and believe me it is fun!
Online play is done through dedicated servers and also includes the ability to create your own server on your PC using the included server.exe which is a rare thing these days and I applaud the developer Paul Hart for designing the game around this option from day one. It is both refreshing and inspiring to see more indie developers do this. Online play through either the dedicated or personal server is fast and easy to use from my pre-release tests and due to the inclusion of the server.exe I see no reason why this should not continue.
Often overlooked in indie games is the audio and whilst the actual audio options are simplistic for Fistful of Gun the actual music, audio clips and voice acting are not. There is an inspired choice of musical style here that jumps from excellent heavy rock when needed to a more traditional Ennio Morricone spaghetti western theme that invokes even more memories of those classical movies. The voices used, whilst a small selection fit the genre perfectly too and just help to make the game feel like one of the most complete experiences I have had in many years.
The options are somewhat basic with little choice in resolution or effects but like many games of this ilk they really are not needed and will max out on virtually any PC from the last three to four years with ease with an option to drop the quality for older machines whilst still looking and playing gloriously.
Released for Windows PC that also includes a raft of Steam achievements and trading cards this game is an absolute steal and my biggest must buy of 2015.
Strap on your belt, load up your six shooter. There is a new Multiplayer Game Of The Year and it is called A Fistful of Gun – For a Few Gun More.
Buy this game, now!

Nostalgic is the feeling that you should get when playing this fantastic game. This is the squeal to the famed and fantastic game, Star Wars Battlefront (1). The campaign takes place in the mid-late Clone Wars era. You play as a battle-hardened soldier from the 501st legion (aka Vader's Fist) lead by Jedi Knight/General Anakin Skywalker. The campaign takes you through multiple planets and systems such as: Mygeeto, Kashyyyk,  Felucia, Utapau, Kamino, Hoth, The Death Star and many other planets/battle grounds. Not only can you play as Clone Troopers, Droids, Rebels and Storm Troopers, but you can also play as many different Jedi and Sith. Gameplay wise, you are able to play as 6 Different Classes. These include: Normal Infantry, Heavy, Scout, Engineer, Special class 1, Special class 2 and Jedi/Sith (You will need to unlock these characters through points earned during the battle).
Did I mention you can also use and command a variety of different vehicles? From small AT-RT's to Gigantic AT-AT's, these are only some of the MANY different vehicles that are able to be used. Having multiple tanks on your side can mean a swift victory for you and your team. But what if you are going against them? Well, mines and rockets are always available for your use in demolitions. In this Battlefront, you are also able to participate in space battles. They too, are fantastic and fun to play.
Multiplayer wise, the Game Spy severs for this game have been shut down. Although, don't give up your hope. Third Party hosts such as Game Ranger allow you to host and join servers set up by other people. This can still supply you and your friends with the nostalgia received from this amazing game. Here is the Game Ranger site:
Even the best games have a few little flaws here and there. A few things I think that should've been included in this game  can include more squad commands. In the previous Battlefront, there were 4 commands. They include; 'Follow Me', 'Move out', 'Hold Position' and 'At Ease'. These squad commands can prove to be extremely helpful for strategically capturing command posts and ultimately, winning battles. It also would've been good if they added commands for star fighters. For example, if you pressed the 'Follow Me' key, the fighter you were looking at would start following you and so on.
All in all, this game is very fun, balanced and extremely enjoyable for both Star Wars and Non-Star Wars fans alike. I can't wait for the next Battlefront game. If you do at any time, get bored of the same maps, you can always download mods from the Battlefront community. They can supply you and your friends with an endless amount of fun! I'll give this game a 10/10, it's absolutely fabulous! If you are a Star Wars fan and haven't got it yet, buy it immediately!
