I have mixed feelings about this game. I adore it, but I'm not sure I would truly recommend it to anyone, especially not outside of the 'video games are art' crowd. I don't think I could justify buying it at full price even then, but I will say despite being only two hours long it's worth a $10-$13 pricetag.
It looks exactly like its art, and the gameplay is informed by the story (and the story informed by the gameplay), which I love. The biggest complaint I see is the walking speed, and there were a couple times I felt the spirit of that complaint, but overall the walking speed gave me time to think about what was happening in the game, how it made very good use of limitations and style. I don't abhor time to think about the game I'm playing, and like thinking critically about the story.
Games often help themselves run smoother with small FOVs or deceptive render distances. By having the main character be blind, it very much takes advantage of being able to clamp the values on that, but does it in a way that isn't jarring or obnoxious, or saddening. It is always a shame when a game's world pops in and out of existence, but Beyond Eyes paints itself in and out. I quite like the effect, and the aesthetic it brings.
It's very much a children's illustrated book come to life. I'm glad I played it, but I don't anticipating ever picking it up again. That being said, it will be in my mind for years to come when I am thinking about or discussing video games and their position as art, as well as just general gameplay and story excecution.
It won't change your life, but it might enrich it a little. But if you're on the impatient side, definitely skip this title. If patience is one of your best qualities, you may have a wonderful time with this.

Okay now onto the Cons:

I would however recommend this game to anyone who would want a rather introspective story on a topic that is really touched. Its a rather good example of a case study in how it is we can touch apon contriversial and sensitive subjects in games, while still trying to make it enjoyable.
If your willing to sit through this whole experience, just make sure you have enough patience and don't get frustrated at the constant backtracking and bits of confusion.
Story wise, as well as visual and audio wise, are superb. Its very relaxing and comforting in those areas, yet gameplay wise, its just slow.
To the average player wanting to play this as more of a case study and to ponder the story, this is the game for you.

Beat Hazard is an awesome way to play your music!
Similar to more popular concepts like osu! and Audiosurf; Beat Hazard utilizes your music library to create a unique gaming experience based on the current track being played. The game itself is a bullet hell/shoot 'em up similar to an Asteroids-style arcade with several different ships to choose from, game modes to play, upgrades to earn, bosses to fight and achievements to get. The dlc bundle includes support for iTunes and m4a tracks, provides more challenges and unlockables to earn and grants access to the creation and use of mods in the Steam Workshop. Though the sprites can feel a bit shallow and you experience some lapses in the fighting, the gameplay and music maintain a level of epic that overwhelms these minor flaws in my opinion. With several hundred songs on my playlist, I purchased the game + dlc for ~$5.00 USD on sale and found it a reasonable price for the content provided.
A recommendation if you enjoy shoot ‘em ups, bullet hells, games featuring your music and if purchased on sale.

Grey Goo is an RTS game whose defining feature is its great graphics. It has a short but engaging campaign, and overall a great game. However, as with many other RTS games I have played, RTS enthusiasts tend to flock to the Starcraft multiplayer servers rather than learn a new RTS.
The Human and Beta factions develop in a familiar manner, but the game introduces a Goo faction that does not develop using traditional structures. All units are spawned from "mother goo" units, which leech resources from the map (catalyst pools). Due to how the game treats the Goo unit production, microing these units is quite different, and it may take time to get used to it. A fourth faction (Shroud) exists in multiplayer, and I hope there is a sequel to incorporate the faction. (If a sequel is in the works, I suggest releasing it as a big DLC rather than "Grey Goo 2.")
The Emergence DLC is a shorter campaign that runs alongside the timeline of the main campaign. It does add value to the story, but you're not missing out much by foregoing the DLC.
The effort that went into the game's art is obvious. The music, animation, and voice acting are stellar. The excellent quality of the graphics and appearance of the game made me question why the game was relatively short and why certain quirks exist. For example, saving and loading takes longer than expected. Also, I would have liked to see the mission load during the mission briefing, not after you accept the briefing and click "Enter Battlefield," where you wait for up to a minute for the mission to load.
Grey Goo is a must-have for the RTS collector, but hopping on YouTube to watch a playthrough would give about the same experience.

As a great fan of the original company of heroes i am very afraid of saying that the long-awaited sequel met my expectations only in a few regards. I played the beta and also pre-ordered at the full price as coh1 is still my favourite game. At first glance I was really enjoying the insane graphics and the well-done effects. The gameplay in both campagne and skirmish made a lot of fun and I spent hours for hours playing.
Sadly the huge amount of charged commanders and dlcs are truely ruining the game bit by bit. You aren't able to create commanders for sp or change units like in coh tov. That means that the gameplay gets boring because of the lack of innovations as most commanders don't differ in significant points. In mp you will then be smashed by people spending money in overpowered commanders.
Although the recently introduced workshop now offers new maps from the dedicated community the developers and publishers theirselfes missed the spirit of the original coh. It's not totally about playing with mods which, like blitzkrieg or eastern front, enlarge the future fun. The more the fact is that I feel fooled by the payable content which makes a tactically based, skill affording game to a pay2win title.
I agree with the reviews which say there are units missing for important roles on the battlefield which, combined with the poor popcap balance, leads to specific unit spamming in order to win the battle. You always have the feeling there's something missing.
I really hope there will never be a part 3 of coh as the vanilla first part still gives more options and a deeper tactical gameplay as coh2 could ever reach in the way the developers behave at the moment.
Buy this game if you own a strong computer to enjoy the graphics and like to experience a nice idea of realtime strategy. Due to the new community maps there's now also some nice comp stomp action available.
But you better reinstall coh1 if you expect a worthy sequel which justified the long wait.
Believe me that I would love to and will directly write a new review if this game gets back the good old roots.
-------
Update (9 months later...):
Well, it seems that now is the time to edit my review. The reason is the Western Front Armies content which really lifts the game to another level.
At first glance the additional factions seemed to be another way of just making money. Nevertheless I wanted to give them a try and preordered both nations.
After a few skirmish matches I realised that this DLC was just that content I was missing since the release of COH 2. Both nations offer a very much deeper tactical gameplay compared to the standard axis and russians. You can't rely on huge tank rushs or beasty ISU-152s. It is crucial to level up your units, find balanced attack forces and use the unit perks. While the OKW imo is great for defensive gameplay the american commanders require more skill but offer more fun.

I really wanted to give this game a positive review.
Just the idea is neat. The pastel colors are vibrant and the feature of revealing the world through other senses than eyesight could have worked so well. Sadly this is one of the instances of a game where execution didn't live up to the concept.
The game is a walking simulator so it's natural not to expect much in terms of gameplay here but it's lacking in almost everything. There's no idea to tell which objects are interactable since there's no prompts. I know they were going for a minimalistic look and the lack of UI could be appealing but they still managed to visualize the "threatening" sound well with color palette change and a few animated streaks of bleak colors. I doubt the creators couldn't invent *something* to make it easier for the player to tell what objects we can interact with here.
Another issue is the pace of Rae's (protagonist's) movement. It's painfully slow. What doesn't help are tons of invisible walls in the game. Not just objects that are there but Rae can't see but objects we've discovered that have physics boxes much larger than their visible shapes. I was constantly bumping into invisible edges of trees, bushes and rocks.
The world has vibrant colors but it's dead otherwise. There's essentialy zero animations with the exception of a few animals and characters you encounter. The trees, bushes etc. are static and the wind you hear constantly doesn't get reflected in the visual aspect of the world.
I couldn't play for more than an hour. When I was walking for near 20 minutes around a fence to grab a ball for some girl, only to realize I'll now how to backtrack at a painfully slow tempo to give it back to her I gave up. It's just not fun.
It's a real shame cause I do see potential for more - at least ideas wise - from the dev team. If the game sold well enough, I hope they take this criticism and try again.
But as it is now, it's not a game I enjoy.

And scary things (crows, dogs, ...) have mostly invisible boundaries. So expect a LOT of stop-turn-go.
Last, there are the gimmicks added for drama: rain causing memory loss in chapter 5 so Rae forgets what the world looks like beyond the immediate 2m/6ft radius, or the maze like walls in chapter 6, which are frustrating at first because they don't make sense, which gets replaces with anger when the truth is revealed because that frustration could have been avoided if Rae had figured out it immediately like for every thing else.

Typical Telltale fare, I recommend it, but it really is an average game. Also the Illusion of choice is getting old, the game is for the most part still on rails and major choices simply do not matter in the end. I had bought both Walking deads when they had completed and that made a huge difference to my enjoyment to this.  It is not an issue for those buying this game now, but know in the future it was a huge sore point to have it episodic.
The story was intruging enough though and well acted, and fit in well with the Game of Thrones TV series (not so much the book).  They have many of the original actors lending their voices to the game which made the game fun, though also created situations where you knew you were ultimately win or lose based on the story we all ready know in the show.
As I said, I recommend it but if Telltale comes out with more of this, I will not be buying it.
They need:
1. - a new engine, new art style
2. - Choices that matter, not just characters replacing other characters after a bad/good choice.  Actual story BRANCHES.

It's like I want to write the longest review of my life on this game, because I've enjoyed this game the most of all the things I've experienced. I mean, you all can relate when the game you want to talk about is your number one. There are not enough words/pages to do justice to all the hours and love you have put into the product.
Look, this game is pure quality.
For all you on a look-out for a quality-filled ARPG title ala. Diabo, Torchlight, Path of Exile.. this is the one. This is the top standard and I know, it's a indie title, not AAA title like Diablo 3 should be, but it is.
This game can and does challenge every aspect that Diablo 2 built upon and takes it a couple of steps onward with level design that's linear with little and significant secrets with evey step, similar to the likes of Dark Souls. A faction system that's more fun to explore than the likes of WoW. A difficulty setting that actually challenges you and keeps you focused on your build and makes every inventory and skill upgrade important to think about in terms of survivability. A story that you can get invested in, similar to, again, WoW - the variety of quests aren't too crazy. It's mostly kill or pick up stuff. But every once in a while there are just lore stuff, that, regardless of if you read into or not reward you with xp, and you're gonna want quest xp badly in elite (new game +) and ultimate difficulty (new game +2/final difficulty). So at least you can skim through the entire game with just using the mechanics properly, but that's what I love most about a game. Sometimes I just want to boot up a game that has a lot of depth but I can still enjoy 5+hrs a day with just the mechanics side of it.
Anyway. Buy the game.

I am currently in late chapter 4 and have take the game quite slowly by making all the dungeon plans as I go and grinding for materials, doing quests as they unlock, reading all the chirps, etc.
I am still really enjoying the game and think it is comparable to Re;Birth1 as far as quality of entertainment goes. As I mentioned previously the system remains the same, but is much more polished and the game is balanced better. You get Gear's EXE drive through storyline so you can't just cheese bosses and hard enemies as readily as you could in Re;Birth1, but it's still a very easy game if you overlevel a bit, which you will if you activate the EXP Up plan early on and grind even slightly.
The game looks a bit better than the first installment. It's mostly little things like Gear's skirt and hair being animated when she jumps. For the most part the art style and quality remains the same.
The storyline is not a continuation from Re;Birth1, but is a totally new story. Things like Compa and IF knowing eachother their whole lives and the ending(s) of Re;Birth1 being totally disregarded. The story is pretty similar to parts of the story of the anime, but is still pretty far off. It's definitely a stand alone story. Plenty of nods towards the rest of the franchise though.
I mentioned in my inital review that the game is not as fully voiced and while that is true I've only run into a small number of scenes that aren't fully voiced and they're all optional character scenes accessed through the information menu in the cities. So, hardly a con at all.
The only con I can really say the game has is a lack of costumes and that likely doesn't matter for a lot of people. The PS3 version of the game had a number of costumes for Compa and IF and they don't have a single one aside from their defaults in Re;Birth. Meh. They have plenty of headpieces though. I am just a sucker for character customization.
Overall the game is fun as hell so far. I'm really enjoying myself.

[Original Review from 05/29/2015]
So far a fantastic successor to Re;Birth1.  The system remains mostly the same with a few polished things here and there.
The party now consists of four girls instead of three which was something I always wished for in Re;Birth1. There are four CPUs so it makes sense to have four slots in your party!
The story so far is interesting and I am really loving the darker feel. It doesn't just feel like an addon to the end of Rebirth 1, it really has its own feel of a unique game with a good story so far. The art is the same, but some characters looks slightly different such as Histoire. The graphics when on the field and in battle are improved and the camera control is nice.
One small disappointment is that the game isn't voiced quite as fully as Rebirth was. There are some minor scenes so far that aren't voiced at all. Really not a big deal and most scenes are still fully voiced.
I also grabbed all the DLC and it adds the 900 levels you would expect as well as some trivial starting items like nepbulls and whatever. The best thing about the DLCs so far are three starting weapons for Gear and three headpieces. Mostly they're references to the Neptunia anime and if you've watched that I'm sure you'll enjoy them. I expect that the added coliseum fights and plans will be awesome later.
All in all with just a taste of the game so far I would say it's going to be a fantastic game like the first one.
I'll, of course, update this review after beating the game once and probably again after getting all achievements.

I was excited for this game when it was announced under the Xbox ID program for being something truely original and heart-felt, but ended up being a near 3 hour wall grinding simulator. The problems first stem from the painfully slow gameplay. I understand that your character is blind, so your walking speed is slow, but I have played as babies in other games that are faster than this girl. It isn't all bad, though.

Diablo 2 was amazing. Diablo 3 was great in it's very own special way. Grim Dawn is what hardcore Diablo 2 fans wanted. I hate to draw the obvious comparisons, but it's inevitable.
However, Grim Dawn is... deeper and more difficult, but much more rewarding. Building your character, skills, items and modifications... you're really rewarded for putting a lot of thought into your builds. The lore is very interesting if you read and pay attention, but the game is still fun without it. Less fun in my opinion, but still a very playable game.
The map system is done in a way to make you explore. There is no simple waypoint for your objectives. You'll probably have to bring up your quest journal to figure out where to go. Even still, objectives may be outside of the location specified in the journal. I chalk this up to "realism."
Being able to play exactly the way you want to play is definitely a feature in Grim Dawn. Do you want to be a brute and smash your way through everything? Do it. Do you want to be a mage casting spells, buffs, de-buffs, and more? Go for it. Dual wielding? Shaman? Conjuring beasts? Do you want to combine some of these different skill sets? The possibilities feel endless.
Environments are distinct, as are enemies, factions, and even missions. This is a grind and loot game, but it's done very well.
TL/DR
PROS: Graphics, SFX and music, character builds, variety, lore, gameplay mechanics, mission variety, loot system... it hits all of the notes.
CONS: Some of the voice acting is not... spot on. With the amount of love obviously put into this game, it's easy to look over.

I felt in love with Tower Wars concept since the very first WMW (Wintermaul Wars), which was just a simple UMS (custom map) for Warcraft 3 game. And this was around ten years ago, around 2004-2005. Long time ago...
Tower Wars is a strategy game. It combines classical TD (tower defense) elements with a war elements, where YOU are the one who sends the troops, not the AI. It's like taking old WMW concept and creating a game based on that. And, I must agree that it ended pretty well.
It's not an easy game, tower wars requires from you a tactical thinking and the willing to practice... much. By playing this title, you'll need to balance between the offense and the defense, You'll need to decide whether to upgrade existing towers, or create new ones, between upgrading existing troops and training new ones.
What I can say about this title... It's good. Graphics are nice, it's well balanced game, I didn't find any bigger issues, and I can really recommend this game. If you've ever played a tower defense game, and you liked the concept, you'll like this one even more. If you did not, I'd still give it a try, because game is awesome and building a strong defense is as important as attacking the enemy with strong troops.

Summary: The game is easy to pick up, but as soon as you hit mission 2, things become very hard. This is the make-or-break it point of the game it seems. Because of it's startling difficulty it usually steers people away at this point. Why? Because unlike a standard Tower Defense game, it's not only about how well you build your defenses (To prevent enemy from gaining battle points) but also how well you form your assaulting force (To gain battle points). Once you get this idea, the game becomes pretty easy, and then turns into a true TD middle-to-late game(The end of the match).
Pros:
- Easy and familiar mehcanics (of a TD game)
- Complex learning as time goes by.
- Fun and addicting - Easy to forget time.
- Very Challenging Campaign Mode.
- Very Challenging PVPs/Versus players.
- Co-Op works, and multi-co-op works.
- Sticks to familiar roots of a traditional Tower Defense, and ingeniusly making it complex, and hard.
Cons:
- Hard learning curve at Mission 2.
- No Tutorials on how to "combo"
- No Tutorials on "Soldier to Tower ratio"
- Difficult to play past mission 3-4.
- Every second counts, and quick "Analyzing" required to deploy towers properly, due to Mines being randomly generated (Which forces different paths).
- Very rarely, but has happened twice to me; a randomly generated Mine will block an entire section out (Making that entire area useless to you/or out of range = Very bad start-up/random generation that will give you a disadvantage that entire match).
Ending Conclusion; This game is worth the play - Perhaps better if you waited for a sale. Despite these shortcomings; If you're looking for an Advanced Tower Defense game, this is exactly it. And if you're looking for a Co-Op Tower Defense, this game is still the game you're looking for. And if you're looking for a Tower Defense game that is harder than every other tower defense game.. This is still it. Because of those reasons I recommend this game - As no other game has proven worthy of the "Most challenging Tower Defense" Game as of yet, and this one holds true to it's core Tower Defense roots, whilst shoving out the "Easy to pick up, very hard to master" Kind of game.
-V.

if you want to know whether this game is for you or not, there are few questions you need to think of.
do you like RTS?
do you enjoy nice campagins?
do you enjoy a variety of unique races?
do you enjoy an RTS that is easy to get into but harder to master?
if the answer to all of those is yes, then this game is for you.
now in a little bit more details:
the game is most definitely fun, the campagin is neat, and the story is somewhat interesting.
but the biggest selling point of the game, would most definitely be the vastly different races in it. this is where the game truly shines.
if you look at how many hours, i have played this game, you can kind of assume whether it is fun to keep playing it over and over or not. to me, the answer is a bit obvious.
this game, especially when you're starting out in it, once you get over the initial hurdle, everything is smooth, clean, and fun, with lots of experimentation to be done, and a variety of ideas to try.
also some cool, other things that we take for granted, as a standard nowdays, when they infact are not.
dazziling graphics, top notch soundtrack, they actually blend with each other, cool cutscenes, good pathfinding, response time, very simple yet clear and efficent UI, hot keys are rather straight forward, and easy to use even for low APM players and newbies.
of course, no game is perfect, and there are 3 main issues in the game.
1.it suffered from a very poor launch, {no observer mode, massive lags, poor balance etc} {of course all of those have been fixed, but it most definitely, did take a toll on the game}.
2.currently, there are not many active players online, and the developers, seems to have stopped updating the game and are busy with other projects{of course, regardless of that, the game is currently, in one of its most perfect states, when it comes to balance, playability, stability,features, and smoothness}.
3.the units, resource collection and unit counter system, are not nearly as unique as all of the other parts of the game. and they most definitely, could use some more creativity, as they fall more into the region of "bland" and typical.
do i recommend this game? yeah, most definitely, for any RTS fan.
it is one of the best RTS games out there, definitely fun, and cool to play with.
even for people, who are new to the RTS world, this game, can serve, as a very fun playthrough.
{something that i didn't know where to fit into my review, but, they got epic units, like, that is just epic <3}.

I really wanted to like Grey goo, but alas...it just doesn't do it for me. It's probably me (and my PC), but the cons just outweigh the pros. I find myself forcing to give this game more chances, and that just isn't a good thing when it comes to games. :-(
On the plus side, you've got all the things that make RTS'es great: three asymmetric but balanced factions, a base to build, different units with their own purpose that counter each other to a degree, a battlefield and a nice UI to boot. It doesn't overly lean on micro or abilities, which puts this more on the C&C side of the RTS genre (which isn't a surprise since the devs are apparently former westwood employees). It doesn't break new ground in the genre, but that shouldn't be a problem...right?
Alas, it has it's cons. Even though I'm playing the campaign, I'm often kicked out of the game for doing something controversial like "attempting to save my progress". My internet hasn't gone anywhere, but apparently the game doesn't care.
What also doesn't help is that there aren't any tutorials that I've seen, and you're thrown in the deep pretty quickly (meaning: figure out what units do the hard way). On top of that, this isn't the sort of game where you can just turtle up and attack when you feel like it. Even on easy, the enemy attacks often. And while my PC is no slouch, things dragged when a lot was happening (heck...even the cutscènes lagged a little bit).
While the trailer cutscenes look spectacular, it's as if all the budget went there. Between the 3 missions I've tried, it's assumed you already know the entire world (who are those "silent ones"?). Result: no stakes or engagement from my side. It may be nitpicking, but I remember disliking Tiberian sun almost solely for the actors not addressing YOU (the player) to solve the battlefields. It's even less here: some European cosplayer named Saruk gets tasked with things but he delegates the actual work to you in a whiny, unclear way ("connect the refineries to the
, and when you make it to victory, he gets the praise. Christ...it's almost how middle management runs my office job. ;-)
Jokes aside...the game certainly isn't bad. Maybe I expected something unrealistic? Maybe I'm just nostalgic for old games? (I just started RA3 uprising to see how things were back then, and it was actually BETTER than I remembered...and I wasn't a fan of RA3 to begin with :-\ ) But in any case, I'll recommend other RTS'es over this one any day. Sorry... :-(

This game is really hard to review. On one hand I see that it's a touching game and I understand why people like it, but on the other hand this game has massive problems and I can't look past them no matter how hard I want.
The game follows on Rae, a young girl who is blind and becomes friends with a cat who she names Nani. Each day Nani shows up to see Rae, but one day he doesn't show up and you venture into the world to find Nani.
Since you are blind you walk around in an all white world. Once you bump into something it becomes visible and when you make noises the world also becomes visible which is how you traverse through the world.The game is rather simple. There's no puzzles to solve and everything is self explanatory.
Graphically the game looks alright, nothing too special, but I enjoyed the visual presentation.
Soundtrack wise I thought it was rather forgettable and overall not very good, but I did however enjoy some of the more somber tracks in the game.
Now, the game has a solid story and seems simple enough, so how come it's hard to review ? Well this game has so much problems I almost considered giving it a negative review.
First of all Rae moves way too slow. Now I know a blind girl shouldn't run like an Olympic sprinter, but her movement speed is way too slow which is painful to say the least.
The other thing is the level design. It's atrocious to say the least. When you bump into things you might find yourself in an area which is a dead end, and you have to make your way back to the other path and with the movement speed it's incredibly painful and slow, which becomes incredibly tedious.
The game is also rather short, but I guess that's to be expected. It's around 2 hours long and it all wraps up nicely, but however considering the game is 13 euros I think it's a bit steep for how short it is.
I usually never say this, but I think that Beyond Eyes is a lot better to watch a playthrough online than playing it yourself. The game is really slow and the problems are what detract from full enjoyment, but you might ask why am I giving it a positive rating then ? Well I think that Beyond Eyes is a decent game. The story is touching and I was connected to Rae, so that's why it's getting a positive rating. If you are interested I really suggest waiting for a discount, cause at full price it's not worth it.
Final Rating:
6/10
Pros:
+ Touching Story
+ Fantastic art style
Cons:
- Rae moves way too slow
- The level design is terrible

I really like this ARPG with some reservations.  Similar, albeit darker tone, to Diablo2.  Art/sound/music/effects/combat mechanics/story/gameplay are all stellar.  No serious crashes/glitches.  The open-ness and various fetch/kill quests are nice instead of an all linear plot device.  Some similarities between this and Titan Quest.  The game can be played and enjoyed without getting into the tedious character builds and number crunching for resistances/etc. stats.
However, there are certain builds/character designs which are more advantageous than others.  Ranged players will find that in mobs your pets won't get all the agro and some (especially bosses) will run right up to you or cast/throw/tap you with a ball peen hammer, and *poof* you're dead.  Same with casters.  And when you die you lose a big chunk of experience but it is more a time IRL penalty just to get back up to where your character was at.  Additionally the Saving system is by teleport checkpoints which is really odd and limiting.  So hold your bladder until you cast a portal, hop through it, exit out of the game and back in to see if all your experience/loot is still safe.  Then you can go.  Monsters respawn after exiting out providing a way to farm/replayability if that's desirable.  Monsters seem to level somewhat with the players experience level.
Overall a great, mindless click-fest that may become tiresome as the formulas (and community) seem overwhelmingly fond of number crunching character builds... to do what?  Rinse and repeat.  The fun becomes a stale grindfest for those wishing to play a game using "self found builds" or just picking it up and playing Who you want, the Way You want, How you want.  It's an endeavor in penalizing not merely your character but your real life time as well.
The real challenge of this game is researching the offline power character builds, sinking in boatloads of time, using your calculator to evaluate percentage chances with decimal points, sinking in boatloads of grinding/farming IRL just so you can wield the Plunger of Exceptional Sucking +42.4% suctioning +33.7% splooshing, every-other-Tuesday.  So to offest all the fabulous math I downvote this game because I'd recommend it for short-term do-it-your-own-way playing up until the tedium of the builds/grind/math.

Well what can I say about this game??
In it's genre, it is up against some stiff competition, Diablo series, Van Helsing, Torchlight etc.......

You have a choice of the usual types of roles of characters, from which you have the ability to power up and branch out into different skills. The extra element I love about this game comes from a Skyrim kind of way, where you have constellations to power up to give your character the extra edge.

It's all round game play is easy to do, and the gameis not too easy, nor too hard, the develpors have got this just right.
Overall a really pleasing game in a tough market genre, I rate it 9/10.
I purchased it at half price in a special and is worth every penny, I would've happily purchased it at full price.
It is a must for those who like Diablo, Van Helsing etc...........

I recommend this game only for those looking to invest a substantial amount of time. MMO's are notorious for taking over people's lives, but this one actually seems to be designed with that goal in mind.
For example, the primary method of increasing carry weight is by leveling your Strength stat. The best method I've found is to purchase trading packs from special vendors and walk in a circle for hours on end, which is made easier by an 'auto loop auto-run' feature you can set your character on and go afk. You can even minimize the game to the system tray while this is going on so you can do other things on your pc, all the while your character continues to trudge along. Some people might argue that this actually alleviates the time investment problem by allowing you to do other things. But logic tells me if you have to create a feature to do that, then the game was, as mentioned, designed for a substantial time investment.
This is just the tip of the iceberg, as it were. There are a considerable amount of things to learn and do, many of which are optional, but it can quickly leave you feeling overwhelmed.
But, I do recommend this game because if these things don't bother you, then it's actually a well developed and enjoyable game. The combat is what drew me initially as it is faster paced and generally more enjoyable than your typical MMO. I would recommend giving it a shot if you're looking for a new MMO especially since the price tag is pretty generous. I only played for a couple weeks. I simply didn't have the time or desire to invest as much as I felt needed to, but I feel I at least got my money's worth.

Unfortunately Company of Heroes 2 is a big let down compared to the original. I bought this on release day and it was not worth the $60 dollar price tag it came with. This game has had many problems with balance and large lack of online match options that were present in the original. Like one of the things I miss from the original was the ability to browse all the different games available and join the one you want to. In CoH 2 you can only auto match. Not only that, the only option for a game type is victory point. No more annihilation game type in matchmaking. Along with that there are many other big changes that negatively effect the game like the removal of the commander tree branch. One of the biggest problems I have with this game though is that it is so DLC heavy. Day one of its release there was a signifigant amount of DLC available for the game. I didn't have too much of a problem with vehicle skins (since thats just visual and not necessary), the commander DLC is find to be such a scam. Without any DLC you start off with 3 different commanders for each faction and one that can be unlocked at like lvl 100 so the very highest lvl. However the store had commanders for sale that would often be much better than the standard ones giving the people that bought them a huge advantage over everyone else that didn't. And over time many more commanders have come out and the game has turned into to pay to win. Its just so sad to see a game like this go down that road. There are many issues with this title and many things I personally dislike about it and I can not reccomend this game to anyone, especially at full price. If you want to pick up the game to try it out and see what you think wait for a sale. In all honesty I have had some enjoyment playing it, but mostly only skirmishes and bot games, online matchmaking is just not enjoyable since I refuse to spend money to get an advantage with better commanders. So, thats my opinnion of the game, overall this is just a large step backwards for the series and I hope there are improvements made in the future. Hope this helps some of you on the fence about it. (I haven't touched the campaign so I left that out).

I could tell you about the many times I played through this game's campaign. About Enemy Within, and the chances it brought. About the mod Long War and how it turns this great game into an epic marathon.
But you don't want to hear that. You want to know if this particular game is worth your money and your time.
In short: It is.
This is game about adaptation. About turning the weapons and technologies of the invaders against them, about choosing where to pool your limited resources, or where to send your troopers to fight, knowing some may not return.
And boy, does it hurt when your beloved sniper, the one you've been watching over from the start, that guy that could always be counted to nail a crit at extreme distances. He has just died because you send your fire team ahead and he was left behind to offer support... until a flanking alien killed him in cold blood. That's X-COM. Those memorable moments that happen amidst the familiar landscapes. You'll also offer silent prayer to that unfortunate civilian that had to die so that you could hit that alien cluster arround him with a rocket.
In terms of crunch, the tactical aspect is very solid. A large part of the battlefield can be brought down, and so can your cover, making each battle less about hunkering down and dealing and taken fire and more about manuevering. A flanking, agile soldier can become just as deadly as the one hunkered down behind a wall with the giant machine gun.
A very enjoyable game, with engaging mechanics and a smart AI that makes for very emotional, un-scripted moments.

AW's:AN is a stand alone expansion to the amazing Alan Wake. They are very similar but there are plenty of differences. The gameplay/combat returns but that is almost the only returning aspect. There are many references to the first game and those who play this without playing the original will likely be confused in many parts and miss out on many refences, but don't let that deter you from experiencing this expansion if the original is out of your price range. While there is still a high level of detail, the plot isn't as great in this one. It is interesting for sure, but the mechanics of how it progress require a level of patience from the player. The story campaign is 3-4 hours long which isn't too bad given this is simply an expansion, but there is an interesting arcade mode to add another hour's worth or more if your very interested in the leaderboards. I still hope to see more from Alan Wake as Remedy really does have something great here.

OK, so here's the deal. I won't delve into the actual game mechanics because all the other reviews have done that, suffice it to say that, no, the game is not particularly good anyway.
The reason I will not be recommending it today is because, while the devs may dispute this, for many players it's simply an "always online" game. This means if you load the game it will connect to the central server (they call it M.U.M.) whether you want it to or not. If you want to play single-player you still need to set up a match through the server (which takes an eternity), and in my experience, if you shut off your internet, the game simply will not work. You cannot even use the "launch" button on the skirmishes without it. Even if you're in the game, people are reporting being kicked off single player skirmishes because they lost internet connection. Same issues with the campaign.
The developers are DRM maniacs and, much like everything Ubisoft has made in the last decade, invasive and taxing internet-reliant anti-copyright-infingement software is woven into every element of the game meaning that if you don't allow the publisher to run your single player experience through their servers, you just bought a game that does not run. Unsurprisingly then, much like everything Ubisoft has made in the last decade, the game itself is pretty crap. It's just not great. It doesn't look good, it isn't particularly well explained, as an RTS it feels very basic and limited, the voiceacting is awful, jus all round not a great game. It feels like a repurposed RTS idea that was initially rejected that they could tack on to their anti-piracy stuff.
Easy decision: Don't waste your money, and treat all petroglyph games as suspect until this behaviour ends.

Here on steam, you often read "I like the part where I uninstalled". Now, by the time you read this I will have uninstalled it. Quite frankly, this game had it's heart in the right place, but like an RPG character built to cover four roles, it just feels stretched too thin. The best way to describe this is "Minecraft meets DotA" until you see how colorful and casual it looks and then want to swap "DotA" for "LoL". When you first look at it, you think it might be TF2xMC but when you learn instead of medic, engi, what-have-you, you get Build-mo-tron Cogwheel, J-pop star, uh... whatever her name is, and the guy that looks like engi but has a name, again, a name unlike the simplicty and genius of a robot named Cogwheel (who regardless if you played or not, considering one teammate played him, would constantly spout off his name like he had full memory loss and had to say it every other minute or risk forgetting it) is the only name I can recall. Sure all I did was watch the tutorial vid, then go and be #1 on the losing team whole finding out that either there are damage boosts in the cash shop or someone was using a hack since my J-pop star often needed at least all four rounds of rocket launcher to hit an opponent, some seemed like they could just fire one anywhere in a ten meter radius of where I stood and I was sent in chunks all over the map.
Don't get me wrong, I liked a lot of the ideas they had. A 3-5 minute starting period of building base defenses, shooter, destructable map, not too high of settings, looked good over all. As I said though, spread too thin. First off, it was definitely too complex for it's own good. Complex can be good, but this is not an example. When every character has a unique name, weapons, blocks, and everything, it ruins the PvP balance, especially in an FPS. TF2 does well because characters don't have names, there is only 9 and they are more classes with a character skin with an intro video, and they tend to be straight forward. It would have been far better just to be the same core gameplay with generic soldiers wielding generic guns (probably a variety though, have the M4, AK, G36, and what have you, biggest difference come when you choose between shotgun, rifle, and smg or others. Now, an RPG character that tries to be the lockpicking rogue, the tank, the utilitarian spellcaster and the talker often can only do it better than those who don't do it at all. While they half-fail all those things, the tank plinks off more damage, the thief unlocks all the chests, and the mage finds an interesting way to utilize a levitate/teleport spell combo to help enemies visit the grand canyon. Great view from the top in the middle, but when the guy with the levetate spell decides his arm is tired, the kobold suddenly finds the quick way to the base of the canyon.
In the end, I can't recommend this game, at least not in this form. As I said, a bit less spreading itself around and more focus on a core gameplay would benefit.

Me upon starting the game: "Great, a chance to lead an honorable house loyal to the Starks and see them win in a way Starks never could"
Me upon finishing Episode 1, and remembering this is GoT and how Starks fared: "Wait..."
Me upon finishing Season 1 (Season 2 has already been announced and this season does end on a cliffhanger of sorts): "Well f**k..."
Game of Thrones - A Telltale Games Series is, as the title says...a Telltale game set in the GoT universe. I won't talk much about the gameplay because it is the typical "Telltale" game we have come to expect over the years, a narratively driven adventure game.
The one thing that bugged me about this iteration of the formula is that there is too little actual gameplay. If I had to guess, I would say that over 70% of the game is just dialogue. There are little to no puzzles to solve, and even QTEs felt too easy and not that engaging. When you really play, most of the time you just need to move your character to the next conversation and not really do anything else. For me, the pacing of the game was really bad most of the time.
Also, the game felt somehow shorter compared to other Telltale games, with episodes being less than 2 hours long.
Now for the main point of the game, the story. You lead House Forrester in their efforts to ensure their survival after the Red Wedding, with little to no allies and scarce resources of their own. Sounds bad, doesn't it? Well... it is... and I can't really decide if that is good or bad... I would say perhaps it's good, but then again...I just don't know...
I am sure that with better decisions I could have gotten an ending way better than the one I got. But still... that ending probably would have been relatively depressing as well. Since the beginning of the game, the cards are stacked against you, and no matter what you do, things will go badly for you most of the time. I know that GoT universe is in itself rather dark and gritty in terms of survival, but still, constantly having bad things happen to your characters can bring you down and kind of demotivate you to play further. Because you know you can't really save them or have something good happen to them. You know that even the best ending you can give them is still kind of depressing, and I can't really say that is a positive thing.
In the end, around the end of Episode 4, I kind of got fed up and decided that I will have my characters go down without letting the enemy break them. I knew what it meant, I knew I kind of chose to have some die because I led myself into a corner without any allies, but watching the annoyance on the faces of my enemies as my characters stood tall even in death did give me some satisfaction. There will be a Season 2, and I hope that Telltale does leave some room for us who made these choices to get some revenge and fullfillment.
Still...the story kept me hooked. It was the most fun I've had with GoT since seasons 1 and 2. With the last two seasons not being that engrossing, at least for me, this came as a breath of fresh air. Once again, I felt the excitement of the first two seasons, the fights, the King's Landing political schemes and intrigues, violence, plotting, betrayals, the feeling that any second anyone can die. And that feeling is conveyed very well. Even if it is only an illusion of choice, for me, that illusion was great. I really felt that every word I speak could very well mean the end of me, and that is what I wanted out of this game. And I got it.
I would recommend this game to GoT fans, and those who aren't fed up with the Telltale formula, which is beginning to get a bit old and really needs an update. I will definitely play this game again to see if I can get a better ending, but for now, I can say that even with all the gloom of the game and its other problems, I did finish it kind of satisfied I played it.

Let me start off by saying this is one of my favorite games and in my opionion is definatly worth the purchase.  However if you are looking through reviews thinking about buying this game here is my 2 cents about the pros and cons of this game.
Story (Main game)
+ Easy to follow
+ Can really build a nice atmosphere in some of the dark rooms/sewer tunnels
- Story can be a little bit predicatble
- Characters are a litlle bit dull, none of them really shine
- You have your sterotypical bad guy, which anybody that has played a game with an antagonist has seen before
+/- All story missions can be played with a friend! ...except the final mission
* The story is a weak part of the game, not going to lie, however it more than makes up for this with its gameplay.
Gameplay (Main Game)
+ Has a beautiful free movement system that will have you running, climbing and jumping from one obstacle to the next one with fluid yet effective movements
+ Optimizes the slow motion really well to show off those hard hitting kills
+ Interactive enviroment that can help you rack up multiple kills effortlessly without having to use resources
+ You SERIOUSLY didn't skip leg day, the proof is in the drop kick
+ If you find the game too easy/too hard change the difficulty
+ Lots of gore for you and the whole family to enjoy
+ Wide open map to explore
+ Night time is INTENSE with a dark room and headphones
- After you reach max level and all missions are completed, killing lots of zombies does get dull
- If you have a very slow compueter some of the speed challanges are unfortunalty impossible, due to the lag causing your computer to make you run slower, while the timer is working at normal speed
+/- Singleplayer gets boring quite quickly if your not grinding missions, playing with a friend gives the experience a whole new dimension of fun
+/- The game will start off with it being a chore to kill a single zombie, however when you reach the end-game you can kill dozens easily with all the perks and stronger weapons you find (i've labelled this a +/- due considering some players like the challange of survival, where others like mowing down hordes of the undead)
* This is what makes the game essentialy what you want it to be, have competions on who has the most stylish kills, most kills in general or who can make it the fastest up a giant building, its up to you!
Multiplayer (Be the Zombie)
+ At the beginning you truley feel powerful as the zombie, latching on to a target and ripping them apart grusomely is one of the most satisfying things you can do as the zombie
+ (This is my personal experience, some of you guys might not be as much of a ♥♥♥♥♥ as i am). When i was first the human, I was seriously shaking in my chair, knowing there was an ultra powerful super zombie stalking me ready to pounce at the first oppurtunity he/she/(it?) got. Your character really sounds scared and the sound track helps with that... a lot.
+ The slow motion used in this is beautiful, it really brings out the power in the human's and the zombie's  attacks.
- There is no tutorial from the human side, if you don't have zombie invasions disabled and you haven't seen this before... your gonna have a bad time
- The game looses it's hunt or be hunted theme and becomes more of a game of chess where you know exactly where the opposition is when you become more experienced at the game
- Early game: Wow the hunter is so OP. Late game: Wow the human is so OP.
- I have seen A LOT of cheaters more or less all of them from the human side
* I fell in love with the multiplayer at first, however after 7+ hours of it, it just lost it's charm and didn't feel as enjoyable in my opinion
Bozak's Horde (DLC)
+ Fast paced challanges that will keep you on your toes
+ The Bozak's Bow is the end reward for completing and only bow worth using, the normal bow is a waste of inventory space
- Very repetative, challanges are not randomly generated and so when done enough you know the exact challanges in the exact order
* Quite a nice challange to add, however nothing too big other than the only way to obtain the best bow in the game
The Following (DLC)
+ You get to drive a buggy, rigged with flamethrowers, an electric cage and NITRO BOOST so you can run over zombies instead of cutting them to tiny pieces
+ The new gun; the SMG is a nice alternative to use, the most fun weapon in my opinion
+ The new map; "The Countryside" is HUGE
+ Freaks of nature are very fun boss fights, especially with friends
+ Volitile nests are a very nice challange and for the insane you can do them during the day
- There is a lot less free running due to the maps flat nature
+/- The story and nature of how you play is quite different, whether that is good or not is up to you
* The DLC is PACKED with new content and an alternative way to play, definatly worth it in my opinion

This game is a far cry from a Far Cry game (says the biggest Far Cry fan ever).
With some of the best environmental atmospheres and artwork I've seen, an emense job was done to make this game outstanding. And it is. However after you get past the initial shock, the game is just a tedious scavenge for endless crafting material in an overpopulated world where you can't move 20 ft without getting attacked by something.
Somehow unlike its predecessors, the game suffers from an amazing sense of enemies spawning right behind you, even after you've just cleared out an area. The weapons become tedious and unexciting (and there are realistically only 3 weapons), the missions are dry, repetitive and mundane, the emotional character connections are completely dead, the story is as primative as the game name and the worst of it all, is the ending is completely and utterly anti-climatic. Mostly on account of there is no actual final mission, you just finish all of the main quests (in any order) and then BAM, you're done. Finally, because it was a grind getting there.
Stealth is now even more clunky and vexxing, and since the bow or knife-throw doesn't insta-kill enemies anymore there is no reliable way to ensure a stealth kill shy of a take-down or throwing a spear through their guts which sends the corpse flying across the map likely alerting others to your "stealth kill". Beasts, even the stealth beasts, are just going to tip off enemies, who somehow know that your beast is no normal beast but you the fkn beast master must be hiding nearby.
The key to this game is the "beast taming" - which is all well and good but then you set out to do epic beast hunts and tame super beasts after throwing everything but the hut sink at it just to pitch your new uber beast up against a single "heavy" tribesman and watch the ****ing thing lose to a single man! Which isn't so bad, considering a sabertooth tiger will die to a fkn honey badger (I guess that is true to Far Cry's demonic honey baders that make the killer rabbit from monty python look tame).
The crafting items required and skills in this game have been expanded considerably, which leads you to spend forever collecting♥♥♥♥♥♥ So much so that the game offers you an option to disable the loot and collection animations to speed things up.
I wanted to open this review with:
In Far Cry 4, you ride into battle on an elephant. If Far Cry Primal, you ride into battle on a sabertooth tiger.
Catch is, the riding of beasts is just a gimmick to compensate for a lack of vehicles to get around. Don't actually ride into battle on a sabertooth tiger. You'll both die in no time. I long my signature silenced Shredder and grenade launcher back.
Respect to Ubi for the hard work in this game, they've done an amazing job. It just didn't work out.

X-Com is a brilliant emulation of the turn based squad tactical RPG genre carved out by it's predecessors. It's charm relies on interjecting the risk assessment and random chance of rogue-likes with the strategical certainty of turn based RPG/Strategies.
While the statistics of your soldiers, their odds of hitting or being hit, the untimeliness of random attacks and panic all rely on chance, many of the opportunities to react to these dilemmas rest in sound strategic decision making. You can upgrade and choose skills, allocate funds to a myriad of improvements to the squad technology or base, and determine the plan of attack when the time comes to face your alien aggressors.
Due to this gratifying requirement for quick thinking to deal with misfortune, this really is a game with an insatiable amount of replayability. The hybridization between action and deliberation is also a great combo for people who enjoy this aspect of gaming. 5/5

Stunning to say the least!
I've 112 games in my Steam library (not counting Origin and other) and this is the only game so far I've played for more than 3 hours at first launch, because nothing has captivated me away from the relentless BF3 Multiplayer 64 player matches so far. Many might not understand that, but for me that's a big deal. It's now day 2 after purchase and I've been thinking about the game all night and even feel like missing work to play it (sadly I can't though).
The game itself is increadible atmospheric and I feel almost like being in the game for real. Of course some HUD features 'off' like mini map, object highlights/shimmering, objective on SMART, etc. to name but a few as well as hand holding weapon & melee assist (off!) then the game comes even more alive; just don't forget to turn the lights down as well. The feeling of being back at such a period in time is further accentuated with a slight heart pounding fear and tension I've not experienced for a while in a game - I actually felt like I was scared when hearing a bear growling nearby having seen how fast and powerful they are.
The scenery is super lush and completely believable. The physics, the control and feedback is exceptionally rewarding as well as the observable movements of all other life forms in the Primal kingdom as they stroll or scurry around. Initially one is drawn in so much that in the back of your mind as you get carried away, you kinda wish they thrown in a few Dinosaurs but at the same time realize that would be a mistake for the time period the games based in and is probably better for it's attempted historical accuracy.
This game is more of an experience than simply an observation and attempted interaction. Admittedly my setup helps me to enjoy that more sitting one meter away from a 42" 1080p monitor with dual GTX970M SLI's running the game 60fps at High setting, using Xbox One Elite controller and last but not least and probably one of the most contributing factors a Sony Pulse headset for that added reverberation rumble type sub low end bass - i.e. in BF3 I use to just hear the tanks fire and Heli blades chop the air, but with the Sony Pulse headphones, I 'feel' the Heli blades chop the air and Tank shells letting rip as the sounds from the Sony Pulse's reverberate your skull; because a game is both a visual and sound experience I can honestly say that the these headphones are one off, if not the most prized accessories in a gaming setup as they make games become more alive (gave up HD25's for these).

I feel so awful about this game. I'm extremely torn. And it sucks that I have to write such an awkward, ambiguous review.
While I do enjoy the game tremendously and was having tons of fun to start, I quickly found myself reeling with unexpected bouts of headaches and vertigo that lasted overnight after playing. As far as I can tell, there is no way to lower the visual effects low enough to safe levels to allow me to play comfortably. Due to this, I'm currently pending a refund on this otherwise fun, entertaining game.
This caught me massively off-guard, as I have never had a history of vertigo, seizures, or other mental-related issues while playing games. If a way comes to lower the effects to a reasonable level, then I would absolutely enjoy to re-purchase the game, even if I must get it that second time at full price. It's worth that much. But until then, the game may as well be entirely unplayable. It's not worth getting consistent hours-long bouts of vertigo just to play a single game.
The actual game is great, and I would recommend it to anyone who can take the overly-crazy visual effects. This is the first game to ever give me mental issues in only a mere few playthroughs of certain songs, and playing multiplayer with a friend was the breaking point for me. And I can't stress this enough: I'm extremely upset that I am, on a physical level, unable to play this game. I
to be able to play this game so much. The few playthroughs before the vertigo kicked in were extremely fun and cathartic. The enemies legitimately got challenging during faster paced songs. The aesthetics are beautiful and it's clear that a lot of time and effort went into this game.
However, if the trade-off is severe headaches and dizziness, then I simply can't consider it worth it to me. I won't let that cloud my judgment on the game as a whole, and once again re-iterate in this review that I
recommend this game at the end of the day. Although this game was clearly not for me, I encourage others to see this game for themselves. If you can take the effects, you'll find a satisfying, simple, and extremely fun game. I promise you that.

This is a deep, visually stunning game that dares to be different from the traditional MMORPG formula. Its strong points are that it tries hard not to be themepark-y with some success, that it has an excellent, arcade-like action combat system (with optional controller support), and that it seems to offer good PVP. Its story also struck me as less pretentious than Blade & Soul's or Tera's, but that is strictly IMO. Mostly, however, BDO tries to be a sandbox and offers lots of professions and things to do in its beautiful open world.
On the downside for some, there is no dungeon finder / raid-based end-game and PVP seems to be difficult and rage-inducing, also, op classes with top gear are hard to beat. So, normal PVP.
Be prepared to set your own goals in this game, and to spend a lot of time exploring, whether that is exploring the map or finding out how trading and professions work, how combat works, or how organized PVP works, even. At its best, BDO can feel like an Eve Online of fantasy MMOs, but designed 15 years later. For 10€, this is a unique offering.

is a walking and exploration simulator about a blind girl and her cat. As you walk around the world, what the girl, Rae, is imagining is around her appears on your screen. The art is absolutely amazing, and I loved seeing the watercolor-like scenery unfold as I went. This was a magnificent journey and one that I am glad I took.
My playtime was a little over three hours because I went for the achievements as I played, attempting to get all of the scenes and so on. There is not much replayability value -- I suggest you take your time and have a thorough first go at the game and the experience it offers.
Yes, the walking pace is quite slow. I would expect it to be -- you are playing as a small child who lost their eyesight a year or so ago in an accident. I don't mind the walking pace, but I do mind the lack of a save feature. Because of the slow pace, I often found myself wanting to take a break, but was unable to because I would lose progress if I did. It is best to play this game until you get to one of the loading screens and can see that another chapter has unlocked so that you do not lose progress.

Dying Light builds on the Dead Island & Rip Tide add-on games, producing a more refined open-world to explore. The Parkour elements give you a real sense of freedom to roam wherever you want, and is critical in getting out of harms way. There's alot of sightseeing to be done in the fictional City of Harran & it's surrounding districts, offering a wide variety of loot to uncover, weapons to upgrade & errands to carry out, with occasional airdrops with which to stock up on essentials. When the last shards of light fade and night approaches, you get a real sense of unease as the game dynamic changes. You'll need to keep your wits about you till dawn, or seek shelter in various safehouses till distant church bells ring out. This apocalyptic genre of game seems common place these days, but few match it's scope.
Oh ... and it's got Zombies in it too.

I just start the review off with saying don't buy the game. If youre looking for a MMO, get ESO or / and wait for a new good mmo to come out.  I will be giving a list of Pros and Cons.
-Graphics: They are really good for an MMO. They look like Witcher 3 on max but with worse textures, models and jagged edges  because as i said - its an mmo, they cant have the world's best graphics.
-Combat: The combat is really fun in the game.
-Enhancement: Lets say youre trying to get to PvP worthy gear. Youre trying for "TRI" enchant level on a boss item. You get full failstacks by enchanting a bad item and hoping it doesnt go to the next enchant level and reset your failstacks. You then enchant the boss item, and it fails. You have to get 10 memory fragments, which you either have to do braindead easy scrolls with a 5man group, and that takes like half an hour, or snipe them from the marketplace by spamming on every BID which isnt actually a bid but click on this to have a chance of being the only one who can buy this item, with a low chance or spamming when some of them go to Buy when the winner doesnt buy all or any of them in 30s. Ontop of that hassle, it also goes to PRI, so you have to get it back to Duo with some lower failstacks you gain with the same method  as before, and that might fail and you have to get even more memory fragments. Now you try to TRI again. Did i mention you the chances for getting TRI? Apparently like 20% from (not that new) tests.
-The whole game: You play this game to get to end game where it becomes fun. Right? Right? No. PvP is fun for a bit but not for that long.
-The cash shop: It is NOT pay to win as some claim, but it has so many useful things, which are pay for convenience, that its annoying.
-The grind: You have to get to level 59 to succeed in real PvP. Grinding to 55 takes 30 minutes, 56 takes an hour, 57 like 10 hours, 58 like 15 hours, and 59 like 25 hours.
Dont buy it. If you do, have fun while your fun lasts.

The game is based directly on the HBO TV-show. So the story canon is taken from there. You don't get to play as characters from the show, but instead as five different members of the House Forrester. You get to interact with some of the show's cast. For example Cersei and Tyrion, all the familiar characters are modeled and voiced by the real actors. The voice acting is ofcourse great by actors in the show, but everyone else does their job well too. Character models look decent, but there is plenty of clunky animation and blurry backgrounds. They were going after watercolored look, but didn't quite pull it off.
Just like earlier Telltale games, it's heavy on narrative and light on gameplay. You get to make choices in dialogue quite often, but rarely it seemed to have long lasting effects. Story does justice to the tv-show by being brutal, dark and full of surprises. Combat is done by quick time events and doesn't really bring anything new or refreshing to the table.
If you are fan of the show (and books) or a fan of telltale games, you might want to give the game a chance. Im fan of both, so I got enjoyment out of it. The story takes place at the end of 3rd season in the show, so there will be some spoilers. All stories in the game won't fully conclude in this first season. Second season for the game is already confirmed.

I played hundreds of games, and I can say one thing with certainty - FTL has the highest replayability of them all.
The gameplay is fun, diverse, challenging and rewarding. Every ship plays differently, every game plays differently. If you like achievements, collecting them all will provide you with entirely different challenges and experiences.
It's refreshing to see a game which doesn't shy away from being challenging. You won't find checkpoints or auto-regenerating health. In fact, you won't even be able to save the game from start to finish. And yet, even if you die horribly, the first thing you want to do is try again.
The controls are simple and intuitive. You can play with just your mouse, though using keyboard shortcuts and the pause button will allow you to react better to emergencies.
The sci-fi setting is a big plus for me. While the story of the game is not explained in much detail (intended for players to fill in the blanks themselves), the lore is rather detailed for such a game. Since most non-combat interactions are done through text, this game feels more like reading a book than watching a movie. Which is a good thing for me, as well as for everyone with rich imagination. :)
The music of FTL has received many awards, and justly so. It is very smooth and fitting, enhancing the gameplay immensely. If you can afford to buy the soundtrack - buy it, and you will not regret it.
Last but not the least, the developers of FTL released a free DLC with a whole bunch of new stuff. You read me right - an absolutely free downloadable content. They could have easily packaged it and sold for an extra 5$, but they didn't. The developers have clearly not made this game for profit, but simply because they like making games, and wanted to share their game with others. In the era where so many game companies use DLCs for quick cash grabs, Subset Games deserve respect and admiration.
I highly recommend this game. The enjoyment I got from it is worth much more than the 10$ I paid.

As an RTS player I had a fair bit of fun playing this. It can be quite challenging to the point where i feel it presumes you have atleast a bit of RTS experience, but can still be fun to beginners with graphics and atmosphere.
Campaign : Had a good story to it and playing through the levels was a bit challenging first run-through even for me, but that can be a downfall cause it works off a trigger. Makes you have to play a certain way, not allowed to multi-task and try rush through the mission (i.e. A mission creates 2 epic units that come at you if you reach certain point on map, i didn't macro to epic units so it was game over. You are forced to make epic units before that point pretty much. And killing them was a "bonus" which i felt was impossible to avoid if wanted to win.. bonus my ***). look forward to go through it on hard later though. The levels might feel a bit the same with the terrain, but for what the game is, the objectives kept it flowing in line with the story. The voice acting was a bit comical to me with saruk and betas, like a south-african accent(?). Sounded odd to what i would envision them to sound like. The cutscenes had better than andromeda animation, not hard to beat but well done.
Challenge: The game is challenging, i did a skirmish vs just easy and i decided to tech up too early first game and even "easy" ai can get the better of you. "stupid goo" >.< . So i'm sure there is a lot more challenge and practice i can do with the increasing ai difficulty before play ladder. Game can suffice 200+ apm, not sitting around. Can be quite fast paced and the games don't go on for ages, average can be 10-20mins (even if they turtle, can macro where the resources are coming in like crazy and the mass of army you produce will overwhelm even "imba" beta walls :P)
Graphics : Can't complain here, neat looking bases.
Mechanics : Here we go, maybe most important to me. The hotkeys work, base and army on whatever you want. I'm also glad they have base camera keys implemented that i utilise here and there to play with. It is a shame though it doesn't work like starcraft exactly (but close), i think every RTS game should. Like when i have my army and i want to split off a squadron with ALT, they will still be in original group. I have to split them off and then select the original army without them, and hotkey the main army again to make it work.
Each base is unique, i can't speak too much for balance as haven't played so much, but i feel beta walls could be a bit strong but the cost is there to for them. It is strong but doesn't cost bugger all "5 stone" a square sort of thing. I like the human design concept and the turrets in base and electrical grid work. The goo, ever expanding nano intelligence. The name is a bit comical though. And my favourite the shroud, which you can macro up hard if run around with mimic and vision. The Mimic scout sounded cute, i was sold. Resource management apart from the "shroud" is Supreme commander like, i prefer shroud so i don't over-do the macro and now the building is stalled :\. Specific and orderly build timing required but shroud just requires you to have the certain resources or can't build it.
Problem? : - Not sure if there is a way to set the "show map resources" as default, but that was a bit annoying having to Ctrl-Z every game. It doesn't disturb the minimap that much to not be on permanently, or a way to have so. - Creating the human epic unit "alpha" was a bit confusing, had to refer to internet. They should show more precisely in the tutorial video, cause everyone plonk factory on electric grid thing. Who would of thunk to put a tech lab AND then connect the factory to that. - The resource gathering can be a bit odd, for example you see two "pools" but there is also a connecting blue "stream?". Even when you have the pools extracted, can place on the stream aswell. It depletes the resource faster but can gain so much safely, a bit sad for Goo who can only collect on the pools but they can move around as their counter-balance defense. - The building can be a bit complex to get head around, not so much a problem but maybe when select the main base it brought up with building list (Q) , instead of having to press Q,Q,Q etc. Could be Q,Q.

They say the definition of madness is repeating the same thing over and over and expecting things to change. By this definition, Alan Wake is ♥♥♥♥ing insane. American Nightmare treats recycled content like it's going out of style. It's still a fun game, but doing the same thing in the same place over and over again gets old very fast. There are 3 levels of AN, and each is repeated three times, with slightly varying objectives in each. To be fair, the levels are nice; each is large, wide open, and the level design rarely relies on corridors in a nice contrast to the Max Payne games. Still, even though each level is large, the objectives themselves are quite linear, and require you to walk in a straight line through a field, rather than through a hallway.  Even with the recycled levels, my playthrough lasted a measly 3 hours. I got this during the Summer Sale for $3.75, and for that bargain, I can't complain too much, but I would definitely think twice about getting this for full price.

Greetings!  Grey Goo is the RTS that restored my trust in the genre. For the longest time I felt the age of the RTS was gone or going; the issue being that many of the largest names in the industry had stopped making them or had gone out of business.  Then, this little gem came out of nowhere!  I really feel this game belongs up there with the greats of StarCraft, DOW, C&C and Homeworld (there are many other amazing RTS).
Back to Basics:  As an RTS the core mechanics are very classic, the style of the units, their movement and how brutal the battles are.  There are some very large battles (mind you not as big as the TA series) and none of the units have really much to micro.  Gone are the activatable abilities and skillshots that seem to be popular.  Thankfully the game does maintain a modern approach to controls having queue commands, production queues and even short cuts for almost everything.  One interesting thing I found was the shortcuts for buildings and units.  It uses an innovative command similar to MOBA using only the Q W E R T keys.  This creates a very fast build style if you know the keys as you have to press the buttons in a sequence.  For example if I wanted to build something I’d first have to select what type I’m building (Structure, Light, Heavy, Air, Wall) then the specific unit (Commando).  The game even goes back to the classic ‘wrench’ to repair things.
Classic Graphics with Modern Effects:  The game is nice to look at but instead of a super stylized appearance or realistic approach the game goes more to what I can only describe as classic C&C.  This may sound like a bad thing but the game is polished to a shine, the effects are amazing and models despite being old school styled are detailed and individual.  Even the cut scenes are amazingly well done; my one sadness is there wasn’t more story!  I want to know so much more than what the game showed and told me.
What do I do:  My one major complaint was the tutorial system, it was kind of lacking, just little blurbs of text that you click on to help you figure out what you are doing, a game with this uniqueness needs more.  Which brings me to one of the coolest things about this game:  every faction is unique, from the way they build to the units they create and even the method in which they acquire resources is different from the others.  You have a faction who only builds buildings in attachment style (think Halo Wars), a faction that uses power lines (basically) and one that doesn’t even have buildings.
Going forward:  I really hope to see more of this game, they already gave out a free extra mission and a new faction; there was also a small DLC that explains what happens to another character but I haven’t seen anything else coming out in a while.  But I remain hopeful as they have brought things out in the past.  I’d also love to see more stories, background and just more.  The source material for this game is amazing.
Ultimately this game can be summed up as an amazing RTS with old school style and modern mechanics.  It needs a bit of work on the tutorials and the Goo faction really needs more direction (it plays so counter to the others it becomes hard to see how to be effective) but I’d definitely grab this up if you are an RTS Fan.

Hyper Dimension Neptunia Re;Birth 2 is the PC-port of the remastered Hyper Dimension Neptunia Mk2 originally released on the PS3 platform in 2012. This remastered version, which was optimised for the PS Vita portable platform, is definitely an inferior version to the original game, with less movies than in the PS3 version and the lack of the Keiji Inafune's cameos (and subsequently the lack of the infamous Inafune sword and beam attacks for NepGear).
The replacement of NISA and Gust with RED and Broccoli, while seamless, also removed a couple of coupled EX skills that are apparently not replaced. Personally, I'm still quite sad to get no prinny and atelier references without the two companies.
Negativity aside, Neptunia Re;Birth 2 is still a pretty good game game filled with comedic moments. The story remain true to the original game, which still make it the best of the series IMO. Definitely a must-play if you'd always wanted to experience the craziness in a light-hearted JRPG.
